about: The components of @acaprino/sigrid, written from its source by scripts/agents.mjs. Each entry is a level of the package (the main entry holds what does not draw; then `/primitives`, `/components`, `/layout`, `/assemblies`, and the assemblies with an entry of their own): a name is imported from the entry it is listed under. `about` is the comment at the head of a file, `doc` the comment on a component. `props` are the props the toolkit declares; `passesOn` says the component also takes the props of the element or the part it draws. `types` are the object types those props are made of (a column, a notice, an option), with their fields. `also` are the other names the file exports: helpers, constants, types. `fromLibraries` are parts of Ark UI or Base UI the entry hands on unchanged.

files.about:
A theme from two colours (owner, 2026-11-22: «due colori e poi un accento»): the theme colour sets the buttons, the
selection, the links and the focus ring; the spot colour is the accent, the one loud colour, kept for the few things
that ask for attention now. The grays of the page are the third, quiet colour. The spot is not picked from the whole
wheel: three colours that go with the theme colour are proposed, from quiet to loud, and the engine then moves each
one until its contrast thresholds hold.

types.name: ColorThemePick
types.doc: What a colour theme is made from.

fields.name: color
fields.doc: The theme colour, `#rrggbb`.

fields.name: spot
fields.doc: The spot colour: one of the three proposals, or a colour of the user's own (`#rrggbb`). Absent: no spot.

files.about:
The eighteen free colors (for what the user colours: a folder, a group, a mark), in hue order (from red to pink). They are medium tints: the color is
user data, the same in both themes, so it holds up on both the light and the dark paper. An app that keeps the list
elsewhere too (on its server) keeps the same hex values there. A color that is already saved never falls out of the list.

Density: how tall the controls are, how much side padding they have and how much room a list row takes. Like the
themes it is data: the toolkit ships three presets (`DENSITIES`) and an app may pass a definition of its own, or a
preset with some measures changed (`densityWith`). `applyDensity` writes the measures on an element as CSS variables
(`--density-*`) and the id as `data-density`; `styles/theme.css` turns them into the tokens the components use
(`--control-md`, `--pad-md`, `--row-height`…), with `normal` as the value before any script runs and 44px as the
floor of every control and row with a coarse pointer.

files.about:
A theme from two colours, and the accents that go with a base colour (owner, 2026-11-22: «due colori: la base, che
di suo è il bianco ma si può cambiare, portata sulle tonalità chiarissime, e un accento scelto con i principi della
colorimetria, suggerito in automatico»).
- The base is the page. Whatever colour is chosen, only its hue stays: it is brought to a very light tone (an OKLCH
  lightness of 0.985 and a chroma of 0.018 at most), so the page is a white with a breath of that colour and the text
  keeps its contrast. No base, or a gray one, is the neutral white. In dark the same hue is a very dark tone.
- The accent is what the eye is led by (R2). It is not picked from the whole wheel: from the base's hue the classical
  harmonies give the hues that go with it, all on one wheel, OKLCH's, where equal turns are equal steps for the eye:
  the split complement (150° to either side), the complement (180°), the triad (120°), the neighbours (30°) and the
  base's own hue. Each is drawn at the lightness and saturation of a button, inside what a screen can show.
- They are ranked. A split complement comes first: it is clearly another colour without the vibration of the exact
  opposite. A hue that would read as the red of an error is moved out of its room and ranked lower, and one beside
  the green of success or the amber of a warning loses a little: an accent must never be taken for a status. A hue
  between yellow and lime loses more: yellow is itself only when it is light, and at the lightness a button needs
  under its label it turns to olive.
A white or gray base has no hue to start from: the proposals are then eight hues spread round the wheel, the blue
first. The theme engine then moves every colour until its contrast thresholds hold, as for any theme.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: Stable for a base: `split+150`, `mono`, `spread-264`.

fields.name: turn
fields.doc: How far round the wheel from the base's hue, in degrees. Zero for `mono` and for `spread`.

fields.name: color
fields.doc: The accent, `#rrggbb`.

fields.name: recommended
fields.doc: The first of the list: what the toolkit would choose.

fields.name: moved
fields.doc: The hue fell in the red of errors and was moved out of it.

types.name: DuoPick
types.doc: What a theme of two colours is made from.

fields.name: base
fields.doc: The base: the colour of the page, brought to a very light tone. Absent, null or a gray: the neutral white.

fields.name: accent
fields.doc: The accent, `#rrggbb`: one of `accentSuggestions(base)`, or a colour of the user's own.

files.about:
Tints with a name, and the twelve-step scale of each (owner, 2026-11-24: a colour system like Radix Colors, in the
three tones). The names are those of the eighteen free colours (colors.ts): one vocabulary for what the user colours
and for a theme. Two things are made from a name, and neither changes a colour of a theme that exists:
- a theme: `namedTheme({ accent: 'blue' })` is a theme definition like any other, which the engine computes with
  every one of its thresholds;
- a scale: `hueScale('blue', 'vivid', 'light')` is the tint in twelve steps, by the roles of the 12-step palettes.
  Steps 1 and 2 are backgrounds, 3 to 5 the backgrounds of a component (at rest, under the pointer, chosen), 6 to 8
  borders (8 is the border of a control, and holds 3:1), 9 and 10 the fill and the fill under the pointer, 11 and 12
  text (4.5:1 and 7:1). The three tones are the engine's (Calm, Balanced, Vivid), with its numbers; beside each
  tint is its gray (`grayScale`), which the page, the lines and the ink are made of.
The steps are those the engine's roles sit on: in light the page is step 1 of the gray, the sidebar step 2, the
lines step 6, the border of a control step 8, the muted ink step 11 and the ink step 12; the accent's soft
background is step 3 of the tone, the selection step 4, the fill step 9, its hover step 10, the accent as text step
11 and the ink of the selection step 12. In dark the sidebar sits below the page: the sidebar is step 1 and the
page step 2. The engine does not read its roles from a scale: a scale is for a board, a chart or a picker, and no
part of the toolkit offers its steps as classes (R2, R10).

types.name: HueScale
types.doc: A tint in twelve steps.

fields.name: steps
fields.doc: The twelve steps as `#rrggbb`: step 1 is at index 0.

fields.name: on
fields.doc: The label that reads on steps 9 and 10 (4.5:1): white, or a near-black in the tint.

types.name: NamedThemePick
types.doc: What a theme written by names is made from.

fields.name: accent
fields.doc: The accent: the solid button, the selection, the links and the focus ring.

fields.name: ground
fields.doc: The tint of the grays (the sidebar, the lines, the ink): a tint's gray, or `gray` for grays with no hue. Absent: the accent's.

fields.name: second
fields.doc: Another tint for the selected item, when it is not the accent's.

fields.name: sidebar
fields.doc: Absent: the light sidebar (`tenue`).

files.about:
The height of what the person sees, whatever hosts the page: a browser tab with its bars showing or gone, a Custom
Tab, an installed app, a web view, a window half-snapped, with the keyboard open or shut. `100vh` is the height with
the browser's bars gone, so a page that fits it still scrolls; `100dvh` follows the bars in most hosts but not in
all, and never the keyboard. `visualViewport` is what the browser itself says it shows: its height, taken back to
layout pixels with its scale (a page pinched in would otherwise read shorter). Where there is no `visualViewport`,
the window's height.
`useAppHeight` writes it in px as `--app-height` on the root (theme.css: `100dvh` until a script writes it, and where
none does), and again when the visible area changes (the bars sliding, the keyboard, a rotation, a window resized):
many events in one frame are one write. `AppShell` runs it by itself. Any number of parts may run it: they share one
listener, and the property goes when the last of them stops. On a server it does nothing.

What makes a page behave as the window of a program and not as a page in a browser. An app that runs in a window of
its own (no address bar, no browser around it) calls `useDesktopGuard()` once; in a browser tab it does not.
- The keys a browser engine keeps for itself do nothing: reload, print, find, history, the page's source, the
  developer tools, back and forward (with Ctrl, or with Command on a Mac). They are refused in the capture phase and not stopped, so the app's own handler
  for the same key (Ctrl+F for its search, Ctrl+S in its editor) still runs.
- The engine's own menu on a right press is refused, except where it is useful: in a field (it offers editing) and
  over selected text (Copy). An app's own context menu is not touched: it shows its own.
- The back and forward buttons of a mouse do not navigate.
- A picture or a link is not dragged out of the window, unless the app made it draggable.
`ownKeysIn` names the places that run their own keys and menus (a terminal, a code editor): there nothing is refused.
The technique is the one Imago's windows use (its `guardDesktop`); this is the toolkit's own writing of it. The
native side of the same guard (navigation limited to the app's origin, new windows refused) is the app's host.

fields.name: ownKeysIn
fields.doc: A selector for the places that keep the engine's keys and menu: `'.xterm, .cm-editor'`.

files.about:
What a drag brings in, already read: files, a link or text. Only one, in this order of precedence: a drag with
files and text (an email from Outlook: the file and its subject) is made of files. Several addresses together are
text, one per line. Whether a file is an email is decided by whoever receives it.

types.name: AttachPayload
types.doc: What becomes an attachment: files or a link (text is not an attachment).

types.name: DropPayload
types.doc: What a drag brings in, already read: files, a link or text. Only one, in this order of precedence: a drag with files and text (an email from Outlook: the file and its subject) is made of files. Several addresses together are text, one per line. Whether a file is an email is decided by whoever receives it.

fields.name: props
fields.type: { onDragStart: (e: DragEvent) => void; onDragEnd: (e: DragEvent) => void; onDragOver: (e: DragEvent) => void; onDragLeave: (e: DragEvent) => void; onDrop: (e: DragEvent) => void; }

files.about: A row that scrolls sideways by itself while something is dragged near its left or right edge.
Kind of an item of the stack.
The text of a capture input as lines: a non-empty line is a thing, spaces at the edges do not count.

A small Markdown of our own, for a title and the notes under it. No dependencies and no `innerHTML`: the text becomes
React elements, so a `<script>` written in a note stays text. Links are not opened from here (the app that uses the
package does it): they are shown underlined, with the address as a hint.

Inline (title and notes): **bold** or __bold__, *italic* or _italic_, ~~strikethrough~~, `code`, [text](url).
In blocks (notes only): lines starting with «- », «* » or «1. » (lists), «- [ ] » and «- [x] » (checkboxes, read-only),
«# » (heading), «> » (quote), a fenced block of code («```lang» to «```», or «~~~»; unclosed it runs to the end, so a
text still arriving shows as code from its first line); an empty line separates paragraphs. A «\*» stays an asterisk.
The parser is here; `MarkdownBlocks` (`src/components/markdown-blocks.tsx`) draws the blocks.
Below this point the sidebar is a drawer or, with the tabs, a page: the same `md` as `theme.css` (860px).

Optional animations: only in response to a gesture, under 250 ms, off by default. A component animates
when MotionProvider or the control enables it and the system allows motion. Motion lives in a separate chunk
(`motion-impl`), loaded the first time it is needed: with animations off it never even reaches the browser.

components.name: MotionProvider
components.doc: Enable motion for a subtree, including its portals. Individual controls can override the preference. While at least one provider has motion on, the document root carries `data-motion`: with it (and only where the system allows motion) a control's fill, border and text ease to the state under the pointer instead of snapping (theme.css).

types.name: MotionFeel
types.doc: How the toolkit moves: the curve, and the pace (1: the toolkit's own times; 1.5: half as long again).

types.name: MotionImpl
types.doc: The Motion chunk's module: what `useMotion` returns when a component animates.

fields.name: tr
fields.doc: A movement of `MOTION` under the feel in use (`applyMotionFeel`): its time at the app's pace, on the app's curve. With the `fluent` feel at the toolkit's own pace its values are `MOTION`'s own.

fields.name: NoticeCard
fields.type: ({ y, enter, still, leaving, beyond, ...props }: Omit<HTMLMotionProps<"div">, "initial" | "animate" | "exit" | "transition"> & { y: number; enter: boolean; still?: boolean; leaving: NoticeLeaving; be…
fields.doc: A notice of the column: the same `<div>` as without animations, moved by Motion to its place (`y`). `enter` false for a notice that was already there at mount: it does not come in animated (INV-002). `still` while such a notice is being put in its place for the first time (its height and the others' are measured after it mounts): it is simply put there, it does not glide. `beyond` is the place above the last one, where a pushed-out notice goes.

fields.name: Notices
fields.doc: Motion's features for `NoticeCard`: the column is rendered by Ark's `Toaster`, so the provider goes around it.

fields.name: Presence
fields.type: ({ children, pop }: { children: ReactNode; pop?: boolean; }) => React.JSX.Element
fields.doc: The elements with an exit animation. `initial={false}`: what is already there at mount does not move (no animation on load). `reducedMotion="user"`: a second defense besides `useMotion`.

fields.name: ListItem
fields.type: ({ ref, enter, className, children }: { ref?: React.Ref<HTMLLIElement>; enter: boolean; className?: string; children: (leaving: boolean) => ReactNode; }) => React.JSX.Element
fields.doc: An item of an animated list, direct child of `Presence pop` (it passes the `ref` on: `popLayout` measures it). `enter` false for what was already there or arrived with the first load: it does not come in animated (INV-002). While it leaves it is `inert` and `children` is told so.

fields.name: Leaving
fields.doc: Tells whether the child of `Presence` it sits in is leaving. A removed notice or item stays in the DOM for the duration of the exit (100-200 ms) with the handlers of the last render: whoever uses it must make the element inert (`inert`) and not let clicks through, otherwise a double click on «Cancel» or «Sort» would act twice.

fields.name: popCheck
fields.doc: The mark of a Checkbox just checked: stamped once, growing from half its size as it fades in.

fields.name: enterSheet
fields.doc: The panel enters from its own edge. Its swipe transform remains under the finger.

fields.name: enterPopup
fields.doc: The card of a menu or popover opening: it fades in, coming a few pixels from the side of its button. `anchor` is that button, for a caller whose positioning library does not tell the side in time: the side is then measured.

fields.name: landCard
fields.doc: The card just placed in a column of the board: it comes down a little into its place, only once.

fields.name: throwCard
fields.type: (el: Element, direction: "left" | "right") => { done: Promise<void>; release: () => void; }
fields.doc: A card of a deck thrown to the side it was decided to: it goes on from where the finger left it, by its own width, and fades, gathering speed as what leaves does. It is the one thing that leaves by a long way, because the way is the decision (left or right): so it takes the time of what crosses a distance (`DURATION_MS.throw`), not the short time of what fades where it is. It stays out (`release` puts it back) until the deck has drawn the next card, so the card thrown is never seen at rest again. `done` always resolves.

fields.name: settleCard
fields.type: (el: Element, from: { translate: string; rotate: string; }) => void
fields.doc: A card of a deck let go before the mark: it comes back to its place from where the finger left it (`translate` and `rotate` as they were under the finger), settling as what enters does, in the time of a button coming back.

fields.name: pressable
fields.type: (el: HTMLElement, { hoverScale, tapScale }?: { hoverScale?: number; tapScale?: number; }) => () => void
fields.doc: Press feedback on the existing `<button>`: the scale of `tapScale` while pressed (`MOTION.press`), back when released (`MOTION.release`); the scale of `hoverScale` under the pointer, when an app asks for one. With the default hover nothing listens to the pointer and nothing is written on the element until it is pressed. Returns the cleanup, which also stops a movement still running. A disabled button does not move.

fields.name: enterTooltip
fields.doc: A hint appearing: it fades in a few pixels from its button, quickly, so it never trails the pointer.

fields.name: Highlight
fields.type: ({ id, className }: { id: string; className?: string; }) => React.JSX.Element
fields.doc: The pill under the chosen item of a group. Rendered inside the chosen item only; when the choice changes Motion carries it from the old item to the new one (`layoutId`). On mount it is simply there. It moves for that alone (`layoutDependency` never changes): when its item changes place or size because another came or went, or the group was resized, it is drawn where the item is, at once, and never trails it.

fields.name: Turn
fields.type: ({ open, children }: { open: boolean; children: ReactNode; }) => React.JSX.Element
fields.doc: One arrow that turns a quarter when its group opens.

fields.name: HoverHighlight
fields.type: ({ container, selector, className, as }: { container: HTMLElement | null; selector: string; className?: string; as?: "div" | "li"; }) => React.JSX.Element
fields.doc: One hover background for the whole container: it appears at once on the first row, glides with the pointer from row to row (`MOTION.follow`) and fades when the pointer leaves. Only its transform moves: it takes the place and the size of the new row at once, and is carried there from where and how large it was seen (a translation from the container's corner, a scale from its own). So it also glides between rows of different heights, without animating a size, and it has the corners of the row it is under. The rows are found by `selector` (delegation: no handler per row); `container` must be positioned. A mouse or a pen: a finger has no hover. It never takes the pointer from the rows under it. It follows its row: when rows come or go, or the list is resized, it is measured again, and it is gone with a row that left; when anything scrolls the list under a still pointer it fades, since the row is no longer under the pointer. `as` is the element it is drawn as: `li` inside a `<ul>` or an `<ol>`, which may hold nothing else.

fields.name: m
fields.type: (<Props, TagName extends keyof DOMMotionComponents | string = "div">(Component: TagName | string | React.ComponentType<Props>, { forwardMotionProps, type }?: MotionComponentOptions, preloadedFeatures…

fields.name: FLUENT_DURATIONS
fields.type: { readonly faster: 100; readonly fast: 150; readonly normal: 200; }
fields.doc: Fluent 2's duration tokens, in milliseconds (`@fluentui/tokens`, `durationFaster`, `durationFast`, `durationNormal`): the ones under 250 ms that the toolkit uses. The values are Fluent's, unchanged.

fields.name: FLUENT_CURVES
fields.type: { readonly decelerateMid: readonly [0, 0, 0, 1]; readonly accelerateMin: readonly [0.8, 0, 0.78, 1]; readonly easyEase: readonly [0.33, 0, 0.67, 1]; }
fields.doc: Fluent 2's curve tokens, as the control points of a cubic Bézier (`@fluentui/tokens`, `curveDecelerateMid`, `curveAccelerateMid`, `curveEasyEase`): the ones the toolkit uses. The values are Fluent's, unchanged. None leaves 0..1: nothing overshoots.

fields.name: DURATION_MS
fields.type: { readonly toast: 200; readonly mark: 100; readonly sheet: 200; readonly row: 200; readonly popup: 150; readonly land: 150; readonly throw: 200; readonly settle: 150; }
fields.doc: Durations in milliseconds of what enters or leaves once: all under 250 ms (test/animated.test.tsx). `toast` is how long a notice that leaves the column stays in the DOM (Ark's `removeDelay`): longer than its exit (`GESTURE_MS.leave`).

fields.name: GESTURE_MS
fields.type: { readonly press: 100; readonly release: 150; readonly tooltip: 100; readonly follow: 100; readonly leave: 100; readonly turn: 150; readonly slide: 150; readonly enter: 200; readonly list: 200; }
fields.doc: Durations in milliseconds of the gestures below; with `DURATION_MS`, all under 250 ms (test/animated.test.tsx).

fields.name: MOTION
fields.type: { readonly enter: { readonly duration: number; readonly ease: readonly [0, 0, 0, 1]; }; readonly list: { readonly duration: number; readonly ease: readonly [0.33, 0, 0.67, 1]; }; readonly leave: { re…
fields.doc: The transitions of the toolkit's motion, one per kind of movement: what enters decelerates, what leaves accelerates, what moves in place eases at both ends.

fields.name: paced
fields.doc: A duration of the toolkit, in milliseconds, at the pace in use.

fields.name: TRAVEL_PX
fields.type: { readonly hint: 4; readonly card: 8; readonly row: 8; readonly notice: 24; readonly sheet: 32; }
fields.doc: How far a thing travels as it enters, in pixels on the 4px grid: the larger the surface, the longer the way, and always a small part of its own size (it settles into place, it does not cross the screen).

fields.name: NOTICES
fields.type: { readonly enter: { readonly opacity: 0; readonly y: 24; }; readonly close: { readonly opacity: 0; readonly y: 8; }; readonly pushed: { readonly opacity: 0; readonly y: number; }; readonly entering: …
fields.doc: The column of notices (`Toasts`): where a notice starts when it arrives and where it goes when it leaves. - `enter`: it rises from just below the column, fading in (`MOTION.enter`); - `close`: closed by the user or by its time, it sinks a little from where it stands and fades (`y` is added); - `pushed`: pushed out from the top by a newer notice, it goes up one more place and a little further, fading (`y` is added to that place). Both leave with `MOTION.leave`; - `transition`: the ones that stay move up one place or close the gap a notice left (`MOTION.list`). A notice keeps its size all the way: its text stays sharp and the column keeps its edge.

fields.name: LIST_ITEM
fields.type: { readonly initial: { readonly opacity: 0; readonly y: number; }; readonly animate: { readonly opacity: 1; readonly y: 0; }; readonly exit: { readonly opacity: 0; readonly transition: { readonly dura…
fields.doc: An item of an animated list (an app's list of entries, the new one on top): it comes down a few pixels into its place and fades in (`MOTION.enter`), while the others make room (`layout`, with `MOTION.list`). Leaving, it only fades, in the short time (`MOTION.leave`): it stands still and is gone before the others have closed up over its place.

fields.name: CARD_DURATION_MS
fields.doc: Duration of the entrance of the card of a menu or popover, in milliseconds (under 250).

fields.name: ROW_EXIT
fields.type: { readonly initial: false; readonly exit: { readonly opacity: 0; readonly height: 0; readonly paddingTop: 0; readonly paddingBottom: 0; readonly marginTop: 0; readonly marginBottom: 0; }; readonly tr…
fields.doc: A row (or a card) leaving the list, usually because it was completed: the row may have already dimmed on click (the app's row decides), here it fades and closes up in height, so the rows below rise without a jolt. No entrance: a new row appears still. The height is animated without `layout` (see above): the one motion outside transform and opacity. The row itself leaves (it fades accelerating, in the short time); the room it took closes up as a movement in place.

fields.name: PRESS_SCALE
fields.doc: A button goes down a little while pressed and comes back: 0.96 is about a pixel on each side of a 40px control, enough to be seen and too little to look like a bounce. Under the pointer it stays still by default (1), as desktop buttons do, in rows where many sit side by side. An app may ask for a hover scale.

files.about:
True for a press on the bar of a window (`TitleBar`). In a desktop frame the overlays open under the bar, so a
press on it is outside them: but the user is moving or minimizing the window, not leaving the dialog.

Where the overlays of a subtree mount (menus, popovers, selects, tooltips, dialogs, sheets): the page's body, or the
element a `PortalContainerProvider` names. Below the primitives: they read it, and it imports none of them.

components.name: PortalContainerProvider
components.doc: Where the overlays of this subtree mount: menus, popovers, selects, tooltips and dialogs. By default the page's `document.body`. An app that draws part of its React tree into another document (a popup window, an iframe) wraps that part with the other document's body, so its overlays open there and not in the page that owns the tree. `null` is the page's body: a provider whose element is not there yet (a layer that mounts with its children) keeps its place in the tree, so nothing under it is mounted twice when the element arrives.

files.about:
Sigrid Icons: Sigrid's own icon set (R6 of the toolkit's rules; the owner, 2026-11-24: «crea un nostro set chiamato
SigridIcons»). Every glyph of the toolkit is one kind of thing: an `<svg>` marked `data-glyph`, on a 24px grid, made
of open paths with no fill, drawn with the stroke of the theme (`--icon-stroke`, `--icon-cap` and `--icon-join` in
`src/styles/theme.css`) and in the colour of the text around it. The set has two kinds of drawing. Most are taken
from MynaUI Icons 0.4.12 (MIT, `THIRD_PARTY.md`): their paths are copied here as they are, under MynaUI's own names,
and no package of icons is a dependency. Seventeen are Sigrid's own, drawn by hand on the same grid for the meanings
MynaUI has no drawing for, or only one that says something else (the owner, 2026-11-24: «disegnale tu»). A drawing
the set lacks is added here, never imported by a part: a part of the toolkit takes its glyphs from this file, and an
app takes none of them, it asks `Icon` for a meaning (`src/icons.tsx`).

The colors of a user's labels (tags): eight background/ink pairs per scheme in `theme.css` (`--tag-1-*` …
`--tag-8-*`), picked from the label's name, so the same name has the same color everywhere and on every device,
without an extra datum. The chips of the labels field (`ChipsInput.tsx`) use them, and so can an app's own label pills.

Palettes from one base colour (owner, 2026-11-20: "selezionando un colore di base deve in automatico creare una
palette complementare + accento, e far scegliere solo tra 3 combinazioni"). Material Color Utilities finds the hues
that go with the colour (its complement by temperature, its tertiary); the theme engine then builds the theme from
them, so every contrast threshold holds as for the catalogue's themes. Two mood colours set the theme, the accent
makes it the user's.

types.name: PalettePick
types.doc: The user's palette: one base colour (`#rrggbb`) and how the rest follows from it.

files.about:
The shape of a theme definition, and the fonts. The toolkit ships no themes: each app passes its own definitions
and the engine (theme-engine.ts) derives every colour from them, guaranteeing the contrast
thresholds. Four things make a theme: the tint of the grays (`hue`) and how strong it is (`chroma`), the accent
(saturation and hue) and the sidebar: `tenue` (light, the tone of the app's ground), `scura` (a near-black, almost
neutral column in both schemes) or `piena` (in the theme's colour, with the selected item solid). Optional: a strong
`fill`, a `second` colour for the selection, or a curated palette's own `surfaces`.

fields.name: stack
fields.doc: The `font-family` stack: the font, then Inter (always in the app) and the system fallback.

types.name: GlassLevels
types.doc: The three surfaces of a glass page, each as `#rrggbbaa` (the colour, then how opaque it is). The engine keeps each as stated unless a text colour (4.5:1) or the control border or a user's colour (3:1) falls short on it over the worst that can be behind it; then it raises its opacity only, never its colour, and names it in `corrected` (`glass-ground`, `glass-sheet`, `glass-float`; see `glassLevels` in theme-engine.ts). One that is absent, or not a `#rrggbbaa`, is as without it.

fields.name: ground
fields.doc: The ground: the title bar, the bars and a sidebar in the content's colours sit on it. Absent: computed (`glassGround`).

fields.name: sheet
fields.doc: The work area of `AppShell`. Absent: the paper, opaque.

fields.name: float
fields.doc: What opens over the page: menus, lists, popovers and dialogs. Absent: opaque. Notices and hints are the ink, always opaque.

fields.name: paper
fields.doc: The page.

fields.name: sidebar
fields.doc: The sidebar and the lanes, a step away from the page.

fields.name: raised
fields.doc: The raised sheets ("Now", panels, menus).

fields.name: line
fields.doc: The dividers.

fields.name: ink
fields.doc: The strongest text.

fields.name: accent
fields.doc: The accent as text.

fields.name: fill
fields.doc: The filled button, "today", the bars.

fields.name: input
fields.doc: The border of the controls (checkbox, radio, and fields under `controls: 'strong'`), stated by the palette. The engine moves it until it holds 3:1 on the page, the sidebar, the sheets and the chosen row. Absent, or not a `#rrggbb`: the engine derives one from the dividers and holds it on the page, the sidebar and the sheets only.

fields.name: mute
fields.doc: The muted text (placeholders, descriptions, key hints, what is not chosen), stated by the palette, so it can carry the palette's own tint. The engine moves it until it holds 4.5:1 on the page, the sidebar, the sheets and the chosen row, as it does the one it derives. Absent, or not a `#rrggbb`: derived from the ink (its hue, a fixed lightness). The secondary text stays derived from the ink, and stays 1.5 points of contrast above the muted one.

fields.name: glass
fields.doc: The glass of this scheme, stated by the palette and read only under `material: 'glass'`. Absent: the engine computes the ground, and the work area and what opens over the page are opaque.

types.name: ThemeDark
types.doc: The dark scheme of a theme, as parameters the engine computes the backgrounds from (`ThemeDef.dark`).

fields.name: depth
fields.doc: Absent: `DEFAULT_DARK_DEPTH`.

fields.name: tint
fields.doc: Absent: `DEFAULT_DARK_TINT`.

fields.name: hue
fields.doc: OKLCH hue of the grays (page, lines, ink).

fields.name: chroma
fields.doc: OKLCH chroma of the grays: almost zero, just a tint.

fields.name: accent
fields.doc: The accent: OKLCH saturation and hue. Zero saturation ("Ink"): the accent is the ink itself.

fields.name: shape
fields.doc: How round the corners are. Absent: `sharp` (2/4/6px). A value that is not a shape counts as absent.

fields.name: radii
fields.doc: The corner radii in px, for an app whose corners are none of the three shapes (for example 4/6/8/12): `sm`, `md`, `lg` and `xl` go to `--radius-sm`, `-md`, `-lg` and `-xl`; `button` and `chip` default to `md`. Absent, or not whole numbers (0 to 64; `button` and `chip` to 9999, a pill): the radii of `shape`.

fields.name: keys
fields.doc: How a key hint is drawn (`Kbd`, `Shortcut`). Absent, `plain` or any other value: plain 12px text (R5). `boxed`: a 20px cap with a hairline, an exception to R5 a theme asks for; the engine writes `data-keys="boxed"` on the root.

fields.name: controls
fields.doc: The border of fields and of the outline button. Absent, `divider` or any other value: the light divider (`line`; the owner, 2026-11-22). `strong`: the control border (`input`, 3:1), an exception a theme asks for; the engine writes `data-controls="strong"` on the root.

fields.name: tabs
fields.doc: How the chosen view of a bar (`ToolbarTab`) and the chosen item of a segment (`ToggleGroup`) are marked. Absent, `plain` or any other value: as the toolkit draws them (weight 600; a round line under the view; a raised thumb in the segment). `bold`: the mark is the weight and the accent, an exception to R7 a theme asks for: the chosen one is weight 700 on the ink and the others 500 and muted; the view has a square 2px line that grows from its middle (with motion on); the segment is a track with 2px inside it and the chosen item has the accent at 16% as its fill and at 55% as its border. The engine writes `data-tabs="bold"` on the root. The toolkit's own fonts stop at 600: a theme that asks for this takes a font with a 700 (`SYSTEM_FONT`).

fields.name: statusStrip
fields.doc: The height of the status strip of `AppShell`. Absent, `slim` or any other value: a dense control tall (28px at compact). `tall`: 40px, so a 20px badge has room above and below it. The engine writes `data-status-strip="tall"`.

fields.name: material
fields.doc: What the page's ground is made of. Absent, `solid` or any other value: every surface is opaque. `glass`: the window's own material (Windows' acrylic, which the host gives a transparent window) shows through the ground of the page and of the frame (the title bar, the bars, a sidebar in the content's colours); the work area, a sidebar with colours of its own and everything that opens over the page stay opaque. The toolkit draws no blur. The engine writes `data-material="glass"` on the root and the ground as `--glass-ground`, as opaque as its text needs (see `glassGround` in theme-engine.ts). A curated palette may state its glass instead (`Surfaces.glass`): the ground, and the work area and what opens over the page, which take glass only then. It is drawn only when the attribute is on the document's root, and opaque again under forced colours and where the person asked for less transparency. `clear`: the page paints no ground at all (`html` and `body` are transparent), for a window of its own that is transparent and holds one part that has its own surface, such as a notice card that floats over the desktop. The engine writes `data-material="clear"` and no variable; nothing else changes. A frame (`AppShell`) is not for it.

fields.name: dark
fields.doc: The dark scheme: how deep it is and whether its backgrounds take the theme's hue. Absent, or with no valid value: the standard neutral anthracite. A curated palette (`surfaces`) keeps its own backgrounds, whatever is here.

fields.name: fill
fields.doc: A strong accent: the OKLCH lightness and chroma of the fill (the hue is the accent's). Without it the fill is the accent as text in light, and a deeper tone of it in dark. The engine still guarantees the label and the 3:1.

fields.name: second
fields.doc: A second color (OKLCH chroma and hue) for the selected item, when it is not the accent's: the page and the selection are one calm color, the filled button another that stands out ("teal to focus, orange to act").

fields.name: spot
fields.doc: The spot color (`#rrggbb`): a second, louder color for the few things that ask for attention now (what is due, what is running), never for structure. Without it the spot tokens are the theme's own fill and accent.

fields.name: surfaces
fields.type: { readonly light: Surfaces; readonly dark: Surfaces; }
fields.doc: A curated palette: the theme's own surfaces, ink and accents in each scheme, as `#rrggbb`, instead of the common lightness ladder. The engine still corrects text, accents and borders until they hold the contrast thresholds.

types.name: ThemeRadii
types.doc: The corner radii of a theme in px (`ThemeDef.radii`).

files.about:
The theme engine: a theme definition (its shape is in theme-catalog.ts; the app brings its own themes), in light or in
dark, gives the values of all the `--color-*` tokens and of the shape variables. The starting lightness values are those of the approved sketch
(design/bozzetti/lista-attivita.html, `coloriDi`), the same for every theme: that is why every theme reads the same. The colors
are computed in OKLCH, brought back to sRGB by reducing chroma, and the contrast is guaranteed in the computation, on the final
hex values: a color below the threshold is darkened on light backgrounds and lightened on dark ones until
it gets there. Fixed, never from the theme: the destructive red and the status colours.
The solid button (`primary`) is the accent as a fill: in light it coincides with the accent as text, in dark it is a
solid and deeper tone of the accent with light text, while the accent as text (`accent`) stays light.
A theme with a strong accent (`fill` in its definition) has a fill of its own, vivid, in both schemes: its label is the
light or the dark one, whichever reads better on it, and the accent as text stays a separate, readable tone.

types.name: OwnTheme
types.doc: The user's own theme: an accent, and how everything else follows from it. Each choice is a rule the engine applies ("match the page to my color") or a color that forces the result (a `#rrggbb`).

fields.name: accent
fields.doc: The accent: the filled button, "today", the bars; its hue goes to the accent as text.

fields.name: background
fields.doc: The page and the sidebar: a rule, or a color that becomes the page. Default: the theme's.

fields.name: tint
fields.doc: The strength of a derived tint (`match`, `complement`). Default: medium.

fields.name: second
fields.doc: The selected item: a rule, or a color. Default: the accent's.

fields.name: sidebar
fields.doc: The sidebar. Default: the theme's.

fields.name: theme

fields.name: colors
fields.doc: The color tokens, without `--color-`, as `#rrggbb`.

fields.name: shape
fields.doc: The shape variables, with their full name (`--radius-md`).

fields.name: attributes
fields.doc: The root attributes that state the choices that are not numbers: `data-sidebar` always; `data-keys="boxed"`, `data-controls="strong"`, `data-tabs="bold"`, `data-status-strip="tall"` and `data-material="glass"` only when the theme asks for them (`ThemeDef.keys`, `controls`, `tabs`, `statusStrip`, `material`).

fields.name: corrected
fields.doc: The roles that the computation had to move to reach the contrast.

types.name: ThemeTone
types.doc: The tone of the colors, on any theme: the same hues, more or less saturated and lighter or darker. It applies to the accent, the filled button, the selected item and the eighteen free colors; the page and the text stay as they are.

fields.name: intensity
fields.doc: Absent: `DEFAULT_TONE_INTENSITY`. `theme` is a choice of its own: as the theme was designed.

fields.name: light

files.about:

choice (`test/first-paint.test.ts` keeps them equal to the computation); an app paints its own default over them.

fields.doc: The user's own theme on top of this one (an accent, and how the rest follows); absent or null, the theme as it is.

fields.name: tone

fields.name: palette

files.about:
The words of the toolkit. A component's content is the app's: what a field holds, what a button says, the title
of a dialog all come from the caller. What is left here are the few words a component has to say by itself: the
name of a close button, the announcement of a label added, «Page 2 of 5». They are placeholders, in English: an app
replaces them, all or some, once for the whole tree with `WordsProvider`, in the user's language, and again when
the language changes. A word that takes a value is a function, so each language orders and inflects it as it needs.
Where a component also takes the word as a prop (`placeholder`, `clearLabel`, `textNotice`), the prop wins.
The helpers that return a sentence outside a component (`kindLabel`, `stateText`, `overLimitNotice`, `withinLimit`)
take the words as their last argument: `useWords()` gives them to an app's own component.

components.name: WordsProvider
components.doc: The words every component below says: the app passes its own (a constant for each language: the same object at every render), all or some. A provider inside another replaces only what it names.

files.about:
Sigrid's icons (R6 of the toolkit's rules): icons are visual anchors for the eye, and Sigrid has one set of its own
(the owner, 2026-11-23: «Sigrid deve avere un suo unico icon set»), the same in every app: Sigrid Icons, MynaUI's
drawings and Sigrid's own beside them (the owner, 2026-11-24; `src/internal/sigrid-icons.tsx`), in place of Lucide. A
component asks for an icon by what it means (`settings`, `delete`), never by the name of a drawing, so a meaning
keeps its drawing in every app. An icon a function needs that is not among the names is added here, to Sigrid's names, never by an app.
That binds every app: an app imports no icon. The toolkit's own parts take `Icon` too wherever a name has the
meaning; a part draws a glyph of the set directly only where `Icon` cannot give the same thing: a glyph no name means
(the sort arrows of a table, the grip of a row moved by hand, the dot of a radio item, the fit of the graph, the kinds
of an item, which `kindIcon` hands out as glyphs), or a glyph that holds what `Icon`'s wrapping `<span>`
would take from it (its own place, `ml-auto` or `absolute`: the submenu's chevron, the search field's magnifier; the
bar's drag attribute; a `data-slot`; its place in a box that is not a flex box, where the wrapper moves it by a pixel:
the chevron of a select, the check of a ring, a menu or a list), or a stroke `Icon` does not take (the heavier check
on a card of the look settings).
The other packs (Phosphor Duotone, Solar Duotone, Fluent Color, Fluent Emoji Flat, Twemoji), the user's choice of a
pack and an app's own icons left on 2026-11-23; Lucide left on 2026-11-24.

components.name: Icon

medium (Park's is semibold: lighter here).
Variants: `default` is Park's solid, `secondary` its subtle in the neutral gray, `outline` its outline (with the 3:1
control border), `ghost` its plain, `destructive` its subtle in red; `link` is ours. A neutral subtle chip is
`QUIET_CHIP` below, for an app's chips: it is not a public variant.
Sizes: `default`, `sm` and `xs` are 36, 32 and 28px at normal density, one 4px step under Park's md, sm and xs (40, 36
and 32px, which is the large density); `lg` is the default height with a 16px label; the `icon-*` sizes are the same

tokens, not Park's palettes. Focus: the toolkit's ring (`lib/focus.ts`, R8).
A button that is a switch (Details open or not, in a panel's header) says so with `aria-pressed`: on, it has the selection tint and
its ink, as the toolbar's switch has. A button that is not one says nothing and looks as before.
The variant `secondary` is Park's subtle in the neutral gray (R4: no border and shadow together).
Motion, only with `animated` true and without prefers-reduced-motion: the button goes down a little while pressed
(`tapScale`) and, if asked, grows under the pointer (`hoverScale`). The gestures are attached to the `<button>` that is
already there (`pressable` in `motion-impl`), so the element is the same with animations on or off and nothing
remounts when the Motion chunk arrives. With `animated` false the DOM is the same as before.
Park's `loading` state, without its spinner (the owner's decision of 2026-11-20: no looping animation, as the
attachment viewer): a busy button keeps its size and its place, is `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled` (it keeps focus,
unlike `disabled`), ignores clicks and the pointer, and may show the caller's `loadingText` ("Saving…") in place of
its label. With `loadingText` the label and the loading text share one grid cell (`SwapLabel`), so the width is the
wider of the two before, during and after the wait.

props.doc: Renders the child in place of the `<button>` (for a link that looks like a button).

props.name: animated
props.doc: The button goes down a little while pressed (off by default, never with prefers-reduced-motion).

props.name: hoverScale
props.doc: Scale under the pointer, with `animated`. Default 1: still.

props.name: tapScale
props.doc: Override the default press scale (0.96 with at most 2px of travel per edge).

props.name: loading
props.doc: Waiting for the result of its action: the button keeps its size, is `aria-busy="true"` and `aria-disabled="true"`, keeps focus and ignores clicks. No spinner and no looping animation.

props.name: loadingText
props.doc: The label while `loading` ("Saving…"), written by the caller. The button reserves the room of the wider of the two texts, so it does not change size when the wait starts or ends. Absent: the label stays.

A surface that holds a group of content that stands apart from the page: the one thing to do now, the item being
sorted, a card of a board, a summary beside a message. Two forms (R4): `raised`, the raised surface with the smallest
shadow and no border (a card that can be picked up, a board's card); `quiet`, the quiet fill of the page with no
shadow (a lane, a group of rows, a note set apart). The large corner, as every surface that holds controls.
Not every group is a card («Lines and space, not boxes», docs/design-laws.md): a group is told first by the space
around it (`Column`, `Section`), then by a line; a card is for the few groups that are a thing of their own.
Its inside is a pile (`Column`'s steps): what is in it is laid out with no class of the app's own, and a class or a
style passed in spite of the types never reaches the page.

components.name: Card
components.doc: A group of content on a surface of its own: raised with a shadow, or on the quiet fill.

props.name: variant
props.doc: `raised` (the default): the raised surface and the smallest shadow; `quiet`: the quiet fill, no shadow. Never a border.

props.name: pad
props.doc: The space inside its edges (default `lg`, 16px).

props.name: gap
props.doc: The space between its parts (default `md`, 12px).

props.name: as
props.doc: The element it is: a `div` (the default), a section (name it with `aria-label`), an article, a list item.

From SmoothUI's Checkbox we keep: Base UI's Root rendered as a real `<button type="button">` (`nativeButton`,
so a `<label htmlFor>` labels it and Space checks it; Enter does not, per WAI-ARIA), the Indicator with the stroked

only after the user's click, never on a mark already present at mount and never with `prefers-reduced-motion`.

row as tall as the smallest control (44px with a finger), in the text of what is around it.

props.name: checked
props.doc: Checked (controlled). "indeterminate" shows the dash; a click moves it to `true`.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.doc: Initial state when uncontrolled.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.doc: Called with the new state when the user checks or unchecks.

props.name: animated
props.doc: The mark appears with a short animation when the user checks (off by default, never with prefers-reduced-motion).

props.name: label
props.doc: Its words, beside it: a press on them checks it too, and they name it for screen readers.

A count beside a name (R5 of the owner's rules): a number in tabular figures, in the 12px label size and the muted
ink. On a row of a navigation the row draws it as a pill (`NavItem`: the accent on the chosen row, neutral on the
others); anywhere else it is the plain number. Zero, or nothing, shows nothing and takes no room; the caller that wants a
column of counts to stay aligned passes `reserve`.

props.name: value
props.doc: The number, or a text already formatted («99+»).

props.name: label
props.doc: What the number counts, for screen readers («unread»): read after the number. Without it the number is read alone.

props.name: reserve
props.doc: Keep the room of a number when there is nothing to show, so a column of counts stays aligned.

A dot of 8px: a colour the person gave to a thing (a project, a label, an account), never a fill (R10), or the state
of a thing told by a mark (available, waiting, failed). A colour of the palette (`COLORS`) is drawn in the theme's

itself is hidden from screen readers.

components.name: Dot
components.doc: An 8px dot in a person's colour or in the colour of a state, beside the word that names it.

props.name: color
props.doc: A colour the person chose, one of the palette's (`COLORS`): drawn in the theme's shade of it.

props.name: tone
props.doc: The state it marks, where there is no `color`: `neutral` (the default), `accent`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`.

components.name: DropdownMenuLabel

The title of a part of a screen, at the size DESIGN.md gives it (Typography): a page 24px, a section 20px, a card 18px,
a small title 16px (a dialog, a message in a card), all semibold in the ink; or the small label over a group (12px,
medium, muted: «Now», «In the stack»). The level of the element is the screen's outline, chosen apart from the size.
An icon before it (R6) sits in a muted 16px slot. It takes no class or style: an app that titles a part with it
writes none (the owner's rule of 2026-11-23). With `truncate` it is one line, cut where its place ends.

components.name: Heading
components.doc: A title of a page, a section, a card or a group: one size for each, from the type scale.

props.name: size
props.doc: `page` 24px, `section` 20px (the default), `card` 18px, `small` 16px; `label` the small muted label over a group.

props.name: level
props.doc: The level of the heading in the screen's outline (1 to 6). Absent: 1 for a page, 2 for a section, 3 for the others.

props.name: icon
props.doc: An icon before the words (an `Icon`), muted.

props.name: truncate
props.doc: One line, cut with an ellipsis where its place ends (the name of a thing, as long as the user made it); the whole title is its hint when it is plain words.

The hover background of a list, as one sheet that follows the pointer: with motion on it glides from the row the
pointer left to the row it is on, between rows of different heights too, and fades when the pointer leaves the list
or the list scrolls under it. It is for a list whose rows are the app's own (the rows of `ItemList` have it by
themselves, with `animated`): the app gives it the element that holds the rows and how a row is found, and draws it
inside that element. It is the tint of every row under the pointer (`ROW_HIGHLIGHT`), with the corners of the row it
is under, and it lies under the rows: it never takes the pointer from them, and a row with a fill of its own (the
chosen one) covers it. A mouse or a pen only: a finger has no hover.
While it is at work the holder carries `data-hover-follow`, and only then: a row drops its own hover fill under that
attribute, and keeps it without motion (the setting off, the system asking for less, the chunk not here yet), where
this part draws nothing and the list is exactly as it was.

components.name: HoverFollow
components.doc: One hover background for the rows of `container`. Draw it inside `container`, after the rows. Without motion it draws nothing and marks nothing.

props.name: container
props.doc: The element that holds the rows (from a `ref` kept in state, so it is known once it is in the page). It may scroll, or sit in what scrolls.

props.name: rows
props.doc: How a row is found inside it: a CSS selector (`[data-row]`). Rows may come and go.

props.name: as
props.doc: The element it is drawn as: `li` when the holder is a `<ul>` or an `<ol>`, which may hold nothing else.

props.name: animated
props.doc: The background follows the pointer (off by default, never with prefers-reduced-motion). Absent: what `MotionProvider` says.

props.name: mono
props.doc: What is typed is a path, an id or code: the monospace face (the second font role of DESIGN.md), at the field's size.

props.name: short

Park UI (MIT) kbd 102769c — recipe translated to Tailwind for @acaprino/sigrid (https://github.com/chakra-ui/park-ui/blob/102769c/packages/preset/src/recipes/kbd.ts)

components.name: Kbd
components.doc: One key or a combination written as text ("Ctrl+Enter", "Z", "Esc"); a 20px cap under a theme with boxed keys (`ThemeDef.keys`).

components.name: Shortcut
components.doc: A combination drawn key by key, announced once as words: «Ctrl + Enter», or «G then I» for keys pressed in turn (the toolkit's words).

props.name: keys
props.doc: The keys, in order: `["Ctrl", "Enter"]`.

props.name: separator

files.about:
The layout of a screen with no class of the app's own: a pile, a wrapping row, two groups at the two ends of a row, an
automatic grid, a spacer, a part's own place among the others, a named section, an area that scrolls, the body of a
page (or a page of exactly one screen, `Page fit`), and the weight of a line of text.
Every space is a step of the scale (`Space`: xs 4, sm 8, md 12, lg 16, xl 24px for a screen that is worked in; 2xl 32,
3xl 48, 4xl 64px for a page of a few large parts, such as a welcome). No part takes a class or a style, and
one passed in spite of the types is dropped: an app that lays out a screen with these writes no class (the owner's
rule of 2026-11-23: an app has no interface code of its own).
After Imago's helpers (`im-stack`, `im-cluster`, `im-split`, `im-auto-grid`, `im-spacer`, `im-section`, `im-scroll`,
`im-page-content`, `im-muted`, `im-caption`, `im-kicker`, `im-readout`). The pile is `Column`: «Stack» names a view
of an app, which the toolkit does not carry (test/build.test.ts).
`Column fill` is a pile as tall as the region that holds it, so that one of its parts (a `GraphCanvas fill`, a
`VirtualList fill`, an `Empty fill`) takes the height the others leave, with no class of the app's. With a canvas in
it, it is never shorter than what its parts need, so the canvas at its floor covers nothing that follows the pile.
`Column width` keeps a pile to the width of a column of text or of content, centred; `Cluster wrap={false}` keeps a
row on one line (an avatar and its words); `Text` also has the soft ink of running text, the strong words of a line
and the 13px note beside a title; it is cut to one line with its whole as a hint (`truncate`), set in the monospace
face and selectable (`mono`: a path, an id), in a status colour beside its word (`tone`), or for screen readers only
(`srOnly`). `TextList` is a list of lines with bullets or numbers.
`Cell` is one part's own place where the pile, the row or the grid decides for all: it lines up by itself (`align`),
takes the room the others leave (`grow`), or is two columns wide or a whole row of a `Grid` (`span`).

components.name: Cell
components.doc: One part's own place in a `Cluster`, a `Column` or a `Grid`, where the row, the pile or the grid decides for all its parts: it lines up by itself, takes the room the others leave, or is wider than a column of the grid. A part that sits as the others do needs none.

props.name: align
props.doc: How this part alone lines up across its row or pile, whatever the others do: at the start, the centre or the end, or stretched. In a `Cluster` that is up and down (an avatar at the top of a message that runs to four lines); in a `Column`, side to side; in a `Grid`, up and down in its cell. Absent: as the row, the pile or the grid says.

props.name: grow
props.doc: It takes the room the other parts leave: the width in a `Cluster`, the height in a `Column fill`. `Spacer` leaves that room empty; this fills it with a part. With two in one row they share it evenly.

props.name: span
props.doc: In a `Grid`: `2`, two columns wide where the grid has two, and one where it has one (a chart among numbers); `"full"`, the whole row at any width (a heading or a note between the rows of cells). Absent: one column.

props.name: as
props.doc: The element it is: a `div` (the default), or a list item, a section, an aside, a navigation, a list. A list keeps `role="list"`.

components.name: Cluster
components.doc: A row of parts side by side that wraps to the next line when the room runs out: buttons, fields, chips.

props.name: gap
props.doc: The space between its parts, across and down when they wrap (default `sm`).

props.name: pad
props.doc: The space inside its edges. Absent: none.

props.name: justify
props.doc: Where the parts gather along the row (default `start`).

props.name: align
props.doc: How they line up across the row (default `center`).

props.name: as
props.doc: The element it is: a `div` (the default), or a list, a list item, a section, an aside, a navigation. A list keeps `role="list"`.

props.name: wrap
props.doc: False: one line whatever the width (an avatar and the words beside it); a part that can give way (a `Column`, a `Text`) narrows and wraps its own words. Default true.

components.name: Column
components.doc: A pile of parts, one under the other.

props.name: gap
props.doc: The space between its parts (default `sm`).

props.name: pad
props.doc: The space inside its edges. Absent: none.

props.name: align
props.doc: How its parts sit across it: stretched to its width (the default), or at its start, centre or end.

props.name: as
props.doc: The element it is: a `div` (the default), or a list, a list item, a section, an aside, a navigation. A list keeps `role="list"`.

props.name: width
props.doc: The widest it grows, centred in its place: `prose` a column of text (about 65 characters), `page` a column of content that reads as one (768px). Absent: as wide as its place.

props.name: fill
props.doc: As tall as the region that holds it, which gives it its height (the content of the frame, a pane, the body of a `Page fit`, another `Column fill`): a part of it that fills (`GraphCanvas`, `VirtualList`, `Empty`, a `Column`) takes the height its other parts leave. With a `GraphCanvas` that fills in it, it is never shorter than what its parts need: the region scrolls, and the canvas covers nothing that follows. Absent: as tall as its parts.

components.name: Grid
components.doc: Cells in as many columns as the width holds, each at least `min` wide: tiles and panels that reflow with the window. Every part is one cell; one that asks for more room than the others (a chart among numbers) is a `Cell` with `span`.

props.name: min
props.doc: The narrowest a column may be before the grid takes one column fewer: `sm` 12rem, `md` 17rem (the default), `lg` 24rem.

props.name: gap
props.doc: The space between the cells (default `md`).

props.name: as
props.doc: The element it is: a `div` (the default), or a list, a list item, a section, an aside, a navigation. A list keeps `role="list"`.

components.name: Page
components.doc: The body of a page in the content region: as wide as the content may be (`--content-max`), centred, with its margins and the sections spaced `xl` apart. With `fit`, one screen exactly, the body giving way between its head and its foot. The margins are the same with or without `fit`, so what is at the head stays where it is when a page turns to fit.

props.name: fit
props.doc: One screen and no more (a screen worked through one item at a time: sort, triage, a step). The page is as tall as what the person sees: in an `AppShell` its content, elsewhere `--fit-height` (the visible height less the bottom bar's room). `header` and `footer` keep their height and the body between them is the part that gives way: a large text, a small phone, the keyboard or a phone lying down make the body scroll, never the document, which does not bounce or pull to refresh while the page is shown.

props.name: header
props.doc: At the head: the title, a switch, a count. In a `fit` page it never gives way.

props.name: footer
props.doc: At the foot: the answers, the solid one last (R3). In a `fit` page it never gives way and stays in sight.

components.name: ScrollArea
components.doc: An area that scrolls by itself: reached with Tab and scrolled with the arrows, as a region named for screen readers.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Defines a string value that labels the current element. Its name for a screen reader: an area that scrolls is a stop of the keyboard, so it is named.

props.name: bounded
props.doc: Never taller than about half the window, so a long list does not push the rest of the page away.

props.name: pad
props.doc: The space inside its edges. Absent: none.

components.name: Section
components.doc: A named part of a page: a heading with its icon, and under it the parts. It is a region named by its heading.

props.name: title
props.doc: The heading: the name of the section, and of its region for a screen reader.

props.name: level
props.doc: The level of the heading: 2 (the default) for a part of a page, 3 or 4 for a part inside one.

props.name: icon
props.doc: The icon before the heading (an `Icon`), R6: without one the slot stays, empty, so the headings line up.

props.name: end
props.doc: At the end of the heading's row: an action on the whole section, a count.

props.name: gap
props.doc: The space under the heading and between the parts (default `sm`).

components.name: Spacer
components.doc: The empty room that pushes what follows it to the end of a row.

components.name: Split
components.doc: Two groups at the two ends of one row, such as a heading and its action; on a narrow width the second goes under.

props.name: gap
props.doc: The space kept between the two groups, and between the lines when they wrap (default `md`).

props.name: pad
props.doc: The space inside its edges. Absent: none.

props.name: as
props.doc: The element it is: a `div` (the default), or a list, a list item, a section, an aside, a navigation. A list keeps `role="list"`.

props.name: children
props.doc: Two parts: the first at the start of the row, the second at its end (a title and its action).

components.name: Text
components.doc: A line of text at the weight it carries: the text around it, muted, a caption or a kicker.

props.name: variant
props.doc: `body` (the default) is the text around it; `soft`: running text, the body of a message or a paragraph under a title; `strong`: the words that carry a line (a name, a subject), at medium weight in the colour of the line; `muted`: words of less weight, in the muted ink; `note`: a 13px muted line beside or under a title (a date, an address); `caption`: a small line under a thing; `kicker`: the small label above a title.

props.name: as
props.doc: The element: a `span` (the default), a paragraph or a block.

props.name: pre
props.doc: Keep the text's line breaks and spaces and wrap its long words: the output of a tool, a path, a message as it came.

props.name: truncate
props.doc: One line, cut with an ellipsis where its place ends (a name, a path in a row): it never widens its row. The whole text is its hint (`title`) when it is plain words; give a `title` for another hint (the path of a file shown by its name) or when it holds parts. It is a block that gives way: in a row beside other parts, in a `Cell grow` or in a `TableCell grow`.

props.name: mono
props.doc: A path, an id, a command: the monospace face at 13px (DESIGN.md `code-sm`), and it can be selected and copied wherever it is (in the chrome of a desktop frame too). A long one breaks anywhere instead of widening its place, unless it is cut (`truncate`) or keeps its breaks (`pre`).

props.name: tone
props.doc: A status in its colour: `success`, `warning`, `danger` (the destructive red) or `info`, the tones of a `Badge`. Always with its word: the text says the status, the colour only repeats it (an `Icon` in it takes the colour, the word stays beside it). In the chosen row of a list or a table, and in a row under the pointer, it takes the row's ink.

props.name: srOnly
props.doc: For screen readers only: read where it is in the page, never drawn (the words of a mark that says them by its form, as a dash for «none»).

components.name: TextList
components.doc: A list of lines of text, each with a bullet, or a number with `ordered`: reasons, questions, steps to read. It takes the size and the ink of the text around it (in a `Text as="div"`, that text's). A list of things to choose or to act on is an `ItemList`; names with their values a `DescriptionList`.

props.name: items
props.doc: The lines, in the order they are read. One may be left out with `null` or `false`; with none, nothing is drawn.

props.name: ordered
props.doc: Numbers in place of bullets: the lines are steps, or their order counts.

A small square picture of a thing that has one of its own: the logo of a service, of a framework, of a library, of
a client. The picture is whole in its box (never cropped, never recoloured: it is content, the same in light and in
dark), 16 or 20px, with no border and no ground. While it loads and when it fails the box holds one of Sigrid's
icons, or nothing, and never changes size, so nothing shifts. It is not an icon of the interface: those are Sigrid's
one set (`Icon`, R6), and an app draws no logo in their place where an action or a kind of thing is meant. It is not
an `Avatar` either (a person: round, cropped, with initials). It goes where an icon goes: the `leading` of an
`ItemRow`, the `icon` of a `NavItem`, beside a name in a `DescriptionList` or a `Cluster`; a `TreeNode` and a
`GraphNode` draw it from their `image`. Ours: no library; a plain `img`, whose load and failure are followed here.

props.name: src
props.doc: The address of the picture: an SVG or a PNG the app serves.

props.name: name
props.doc: What the picture is («PostgreSQL»): its accessible name. Without it the picture is hidden from screen readers, as it should be when the name is written beside it.

props.name: decorative
props.doc: The name is written beside the picture: hide it from screen readers even with a `name`.

props.name: size
props.doc: `sm` 16px (the default), `md` 20px.

props.name: icon
props.doc: One of Sigrid's icons, drawn in the box while the picture loads and when it fails. Without it the box is empty, at the same size.

props.name: children
props.doc: What is drawn in the box instead of `icon`, for a part that has a mark of its own there (the dot of a colour).

components.name: PopoverAnchor
components.doc: A reference other than the button for the card's position (Base UI has no such part: the Positioner's `anchor`).

props.name: animated
props.doc: The card enters with a short fade (off by default, never with prefers-reduced-motion). Its fade on closing is the app's `MotionProvider animated`, as for every surface.

props.name: width
props.doc: How wide the card is: absent, 320px; `sm` 384px, `md` 448px, `lg` 512px, `xl` 576px, and never wider than the room the window leaves.

How far a task is: a bar (`Progress`), a ring (`ProgressRing`) or blocks (`ProgressSegments`), one API for the three.
Written by hand: Ark's Progress names the bar with its own value («45%») and gives no `aria-valuetext`, and there is no
keyboard to inherit; here the app names the bar, the toolkit says the value. The form is Park UI's progress recipe
(102769c): a track 8px (`sm`) or 10px (`md`) tall with the corners of a control (l1), the range filling it from the
start. Not taken from it: the stripes, the gradient of its indeterminate state and its animation (no gradient, no
loop but the skeletons: DESIGN.md), and the pill shape (round only for avatars, dots and switches, R7).
The ring and the blocks are ours; Park's circular recipe was not read.
The colours: the track is the quiet fill (the ink at 6%), the range is the accent as progress (R2); done is the
success colour and a failure the destructive one, each with a word (DESIGN.md "Status": a colour is never alone).
A failure also has the one look it has everywhere: Sigrid's `error` icon (the circle with an X), inside the ring and
before the word of the bar and of the blocks.
Nothing moves: the range jumps to the value, as the steps do. A progress that changes by events (an upload) is not a
gesture, so no tween (DESIGN.md Motion). The range is `primary`, the fill of the accent, as in the checkbox and the
switch (DESIGN.md Colors).
Not knowing how far it is (`value={null}`) is a track with no range and the word «In progress», not a loop.
In a line of words (the frame's status row, docs/patterns.md «Progress of a task») the bar is `inline`: a fixed width
that does not give way, so the words beside it stay put while the value moves.
For screen readers: `role="progressbar"` named by the app, with `aria-valuenow` and, always, `aria-valuetext` («45%»,
«Complete»). The visible text repeats it and is hidden from them. A page that updates a value often should
announce the end and the failure only, in a live region of its own, not every percent.

props.name: value
props.doc: How much is done, from 0 to `max`. `null`: it is not known how far it is.

props.name: max

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: What is progressing («Upload», «Import»), for screen readers.

props.name: valueText
props.doc: What the value says, in place of the toolkit's words («16 seconds left»): read by screen readers and shown by `showValue`.

props.name: countdown

props.name: status

SmoothUI (MIT) radio-group 4.0.0 — adapted for @acaprino/sigrid (https://smoothui.dev/r/base-nova/radio-group.json)
From SmoothUI's RadioGroup we keep: Base UI's Root and Radio (`role="radiogroup"`/`role="radio"` with
`aria-checked`, a single Tab stop, arrows that move focus and select, wrapping at the ends), the Radio
rendered as a real `<button type="button">` (`nativeButton`), the Indicator with the filled dot and the optional label.
Adapted: Base UI does not handle Home and End in the radio group (`enableHomeAndEndKeys: false`), here they go to the first and
last enabled radio and select it, like the arrows; `theme.css` tokens (`input` border, dot and selected border
`ink`, `ring/50` ring), touch area enlarged to 24 px (44 with touch). Removed: all of Motion's animations (cascading
appearance of the radios, spring on the dot, `useReducedMotion`): the dot is there or it is not, no movement, Motion is not loaded.

props.name: defaultValue
props.doc: Initial value when uncontrolled.

props.name: value
props.doc: Selected value (controlled).

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with the value the user chose (click, Space, arrows, Home, End).

props.name: name
props.doc: Name for form submission; without a name the group does not enter the form data.

props.name: orientation
props.doc: Layout only: the arrows work in both directions, as in a WAI-ARIA radio group.

props.name: value
props.doc: The value of this choice.

props.name: children
props.doc: Text of the label next to the radio (optional: without it, `aria-label` is needed).

props.name: variant
props.doc: "radio" (default): circle with a border and a filled dot. "swatch": filled pill (the color comes from `style`), the selection is an ink ring detached from the pill and focus a wider outline, so selection and focus remain distinct even together; no dot.

SmoothUI (MIT) select 4.0.0 — adapted for @acaprino/sigrid (https://smoothui.dev/r/base-nova/select.json)
Park UI (MIT) select 102769c — recipe translated to Tailwind for @acaprino/sigrid (https://github.com/chakra-ui/park-ui/blob/102769c/packages/preset/src/recipes/select.ts)
From Park's `select` recipe comes the form: its outline variant at the md size for the button (40px, l2 corners, 12px
of side padding, a border and no fill, as the fields; 36px at `size="sm"`; R4: a border, never a shadow too; open, the
border is the ink), and its list (l2 corners, md elevation in place
of a border, 4px of padding, items 40px tall with l1 corners and a quiet fill on the highlighted one). The text is
14px, not Park's 16px (the type scale of the app). The button's border stays `border-input` (3:1, WCAG 1.4.11):
Park's outline border is lighter.
From SmoothUI we keep the data API (`options`: `{ value, label }`, `value`/`onValueChange`, `aria-label`, `id` on the
button), the shape (button with an arrow, card with the list and the check mark on the chosen item) and the classes
of the card. SmoothUI's hand-made listbox (createPortal + computed position) is replaced by the primitive
`Select` from Base UI (Root, Trigger, Value, Icon, Portal, Positioner, Popup, List, Item, ItemText, ItemIndicator): so
keyboard (arrows, type-ahead, Enter, Esc), ARIA roles and the portal nested in a modal sheet come from the
primitive. The list uses the shared Motion entrance from the trigger.
States from Park's recipe (the owner's decision of 2026-11-20): `disabled` is the toolkit's disabled look (half
opacity, no pointer, out of the Tab order: Base UI's `disabled`), `invalid` sets `aria-invalid` and turns the 3:1
control border into the destructive colour, also while the list is open (Park's `_invalid`).
A value that is not among the options leaves the button empty (like the previous `<option hidden>`) and cannot be chosen.

props.name: aria-describedby
props.doc: The ids of the texts that describe the select (a `FormField`'s helper or error).

props.name: aria-invalid
props.doc: As `invalid`: what a `FormField` with an error passes to its control.

props.name: groups
props.doc: Grouped options, with a non-selectable heading (Base UI's `Select.Group`), after `options`.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: The button text when the value is not among the options (default: empty, as before).

props.name: renderMark
props.doc: The mark drawn before an option's label in the list (`aria-hidden`), or null for none. Absent: no mark.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: The value cannot be changed: half opacity, no pointer, not reachable with Tab (Base UI's `disabled`).

props.name: invalid
props.doc: The value is not accepted: `aria-invalid` and the control border in the destructive colour.

types.name: SelectOption
types.doc: An option: a value and its label. An app can add its own fields (`O extends SelectOption`) and draw them before the label with `renderMark` (a coloured shape, for example): the mark is the app's, the list is the toolkit's. `style` is put on the label in the list: a font shown in its own face, for example.

A hairline between two groups of a page or a panel, in the divider's colour: what tells two groups apart where the
space between them is not enough («Lines and space, not boxes», docs/design-laws.md). It is a horizontal rule, read
by screen readers as a separator, and takes no room of its own: the pile around it spaces it. The separators of a
bar and of a menu are their own (`ToolbarSeparator`, `DropdownMenuSeparator`).

components.name: Separator
components.doc: A line across its place, between two groups.

props.name: decorative
props.doc: Only a drawing (between two groups that are already told apart for a screen reader): hidden from screen readers.

SmoothUI (MIT) drawer 4.0.0 — adapted for @acaprino/sigrid (https://smoothui.dev/r/base-nova/drawer.json)
Park UI (MIT) drawer 102769c — recipe translated to Tailwind for @acaprino/sigrid (https://github.com/chakra-ui/park-ui/blob/102769c/packages/preset/src/recipes/drawer.ts)
From Park's `drawer` recipe comes the elevation (lg, in place of a border: no border on the inner edge, R4) and the
backdrop (the `drop` color, at the 40% of `BACKDROP`, the same as the dialog's). The title is 16px semibold (Park's is 20px: R7, text sizes from the toolkit's tokens).
From SmoothUI's Drawer we keep Base UI's primitives (Root, Portal, Backdrop, Viewport, Popup, Content), the
drag direction per side and the content marked `Drawer.Content` (a mouse drag that starts
there does not move the sheet: the text of the fields can be selected). Removed: the 400 ms CSS transitions, the spring and the
staggering of the children with Motion. The entrance (32 px from the panel edge, 200 ms) follows
the shared Motion preference and respects reduced motion.

components.name: Sheet
components.doc: A modal sheet: focus trapped, Esc and a click outside close it, page scrolling is blocked. With `modal={false}` it is a side panel beside the page: no backdrop, the focus is not trapped, the page scrolls and takes clicks, and Esc or a click outside still close it (`disablePointerDismissal` keeps it open on a click outside). A click on the notifications (which sit above, outside the sheet) does not close it: Base UI closes a modal only on what is behind it, and here a second safeguard also cancels the closing caused by focus moving to the notifications.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.doc: `reason` is told when it closes: an app that keeps a form in the sheet may answer a press outside differently from the Esc.

props.name: closesOnEscape
props.doc: Asked at each Esc: false leaves the sheet open and the key to what has the focus and to the app's commands (the `Inspector` beside the page answers it so, when the focus is not in it). Absent: Esc always closes the sheet.

props.name: width
props.doc: At the side (`left`, `right`): the widest it grows, `sm` 384px (the default), `md` 448px, `lg` 512px. Ignored at the top or the foot.

props.name: cover
props.doc: On a narrow window the sheet covers it all (a message being read, a file being looked at): it is then that window's page, on the page's ground; from the `sm` width up it is a raised surface at the side, as wide as `width` or the caller's own `max-w-*`.

props.name: onCloseAutoFocus
props.doc: On closing, before the focus moves (like Radix's `onCloseAutoFocus`): `event.preventDefault()` says that the caller has already taken care of the focus, and the sheet no longer touches it.

props.name: animated
props.doc: Animate the entrance from the configured edge. Inherits the provider preference.

Park UI (MIT) slider 102769c — recipe translated to Tailwind for @acaprino/sigrid (https://github.com/chakra-ui/park-ui/blob/102769c/packages/preset/src/recipes/slider.ts)
From Park's `slider` recipe comes the form (its md size, its outline variant): a round 8px track, the part up to the
value filled, and a round 20px thumb with a 2px border, centred on the track. Ours: the track is the `input` token
(3:1 on every background, WCAG 1.4.11; Park's is its hairline border colour), the filled part and the thumb's
border are the ink (the accent is kept for the primary action, R2), the thumb is the paper with no shadow (R4: a
bordered control has no shadow). The thumb's area is 44px with a coarse pointer.
Behaviour: Ark UI's Slider, one thumb (`role="slider"`): Left and Right move by `step`, PageUp and PageDown by ten
steps, Home and End go to the ends; Up and Down act as Right and Left, as the ARIA pattern has it. No animation: the
thumb follows the pointer.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with each value while the thumb moves.

props.name: step
props.doc: The distance between two values. Default 1.

props.name: aria-label
