A table: rows of the same things, each with the same facts in columns. These are the parts of its form and nothing
more: a `<table>` in a box that scrolls, a heading row, rows and cells, drawn with the toolkit's tokens so every
table of an app reads as the others do.
- A row is as tall as the density's row (44px with a finger), with a line under it and no other frame (R4).
- A heading is small muted text (the label size); a column of numbers is set at the end, in tabular figures (R5).
- The row chosen has the selection tint, stronger text and a short accent bar at its start (R1), as in every list;
  under the pointer a row takes a share of that tint. The row of the headings takes none: it is not a row to choose.
- A column of numbers (`align="end"`) never wraps: a size is read on one line.
- A cell that takes the room the other columns leave (`grow`) cuts a one-line text in it instead of widening the table.
What a table does (sorting, filtering, choosing columns, drawing only the rows in sight) is not here: `DataTable`
(the `./table` entry of the package) does the first and the last on TanStack Table, and an app with a table of its
own drives it with the library it likes and draws it with these parts.

shape of the card (ink on paper, small text). Adapted to icon-only buttons: the text is the button's accessible
name (`label`, the same as its `aria-label`), not free content; no Provider (each
hint has its own delay, 500 ms), no controlled state. Removed: SmoothUI's CSS transitions

From Park's `tags-input` recipe (md) comes the look: the field 40px tall with l2 corners and 6px of side padding,
6px between the chips, each chip 28px tall with l1 corners and its own 20px remove button. What the field does rests
on Ark UI's TagsInput (`@ark-ui/react/tags-input`).
Ark gives: Enter and the comma that close a label, a pasted «a, b, c» split into labels, the text left in the box
added when the field is left, the arrows that walk the chips from the box (Delete or Backspace removes the one
reached), the remove button of each chip with its name, the announcements to screen readers, one Tab stop for the
whole field. Ours: the chip is the neutral `Badge` with a dot in the color of its name (`tag-color.ts`, R10); the words are about
«labels», in English; a label already there is not added again whatever its case; Backspace in the empty box removes
the last label at once (Ark would first select it and remove it at the second press); a chip is not edited in place;
a comma that arrives with other text in one go (an autocorrection, a keyboard's suggestion) closes the labels before
it and leaves the rest in the box (Ark would add the text it had before that event).
With `suggestions` the box is also a combobox (Ark UI's Combobox, on the same text box): while the user writes, the
labels that match and are not in the field yet are listed under it; the arrows move, Enter or a click adds the one
reached, Esc closes the list only. Any other text is still a label of its own (Enter, the comma, leaving the box).

The question asked before an action that cannot be taken back: deleting for good, sending what cannot be recalled.
One look for it in every app: a small window with what will happen as its title, what is lost under it, «Cancel»
and the one button that does it, named by its verb («Delete the project», never «OK» or «Yes»).
Only for what cannot be undone. An action that can be taken back is done at once and offers Undo in a notice
(`Toasts`): asking first is one question too many, every time.
The focus starts on «Cancel», so Enter pressed out of habit does nothing lost; Esc and a press outside cancel too.
The button that does it is red when what it does destroys something (`destructive`, the default), and the solid
one otherwise; while the app does it (`busy`) it waits in its place and the window stays.

A menu on a thing, opened with the right button or with the Menu key (Shift+F10): the actions of a row, a tab, a
file, listed once and found where the pointer is. It wraps what it is for (a row, a list, a pane, a tab) and lays no box
of its own around it (a `div` with `display: contents`), so the thing keeps its place. The entries are data: an action (a label, its icon, its
key as a hint, `destructive` for the one that deletes), a submenu, a heading, a separator. The card and the rows are
`DropdownMenu`'s, so the menu is the one of every other: the arrows, Home and End, a letter, Enter, Escape, which brings
the focus back to where it was.
- The pointer's menu opens at the point pressed; the keyboard's, under the thing that has the focus. A text field and
  its kin keep the system's own menu (copy, paste). A menu inside a menu is the inner one's: the outer one leaves a
  press that was taken.
- The entries are read when the menu opens (`items` may be a function, given the element pressed or in focus), so a menu
  always says what the thing is now; and one menu around a whole list can read which row it is on from that element.
- An action is also a button somewhere the person can reach without the menu: a menu is a shortcut, never the only
  way (a touch screen has no right button).

Park UI (MIT) input 102769c — recipe translated to Tailwind for @acaprino/sigrid (https://github.com/chakra-ui/park-ui/blob/102769c/packages/preset/src/recipes/input.ts)
From Park's `input` recipe (md): the button that opens the calendar has the field's form (40px, l2 corners, 12px of
side padding); the card is Park's date-picker content (l3 corners, the lg elevation).
The date field: a button that shows the date and opens the calendar, on Ark UI's DatePicker
(`@ark-ui/react/date-picker`). Two variants (a form can use both), with the same contract as the native fields they
replace: `DateField` gives and receives `YYYY-MM-DD` (or null), `DateTimeField` `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm` in local time
(or null; the time is switched on with the «Time» checkbox, otherwise 09:00). Only formatting of local dates: no time
zones, no «tomorrow». The button takes the `id` of the field's `<label>` (accessible name «Due date», «Reminder»).
Ark gives: the open state and its dismissal (Esc or a click outside close without choosing, and focus returns to the
button), the position of the card, focus on the chosen day when it opens, the grid (see `components/calendar.tsx`).
The card is not moved to a portal: it stays inside the field, so it is part of the modal sheet that holds it (its
focus trap, its Esc), and `fixed` keeps the scrolling body of the sheet from clipping it.

One row that opens in place: what most people do not need on most visits stays behind it, and the first view holds
the rest (progressive disclosure). The row is named for what it holds («Add a coupon»; «More options» only for a
mix). What is inside stays in the page while closed, so what was written there is kept, and the page does not move
the reader anywhere: it grows under the row. Base UI's `Collapsible` gives the behaviour (a button with
`aria-expanded` that names its panel); the form is the toolkit's: a quiet row with the chevron in the icon slot,
44px with a finger. Never inside another `Disclosure` that is itself inside one: two levels at most.
Never put behind it what people need before they commit: a price, a required field, what a delete removes.
The arrow is the one of every row that opens (a branch of the tree, a group of the sidebar): 14px in a 16px slot,
a quarter turn when open. With motion on it turns (`Turn`) when the reader pressed the row, and only then: a row
the app opens or closes by itself (a reasoning that ends) changes at once, since nothing moves without a gesture.
The panel glides open and shut the same way (`internal/reveal.ts`, theme.css).

«None». The field does not add, convert or check the total: it sends hours and minutes as they are and the app decides
(up to 24 hours, minutes from 0 to 59; zero and zero means «None»). Two inputs have no syntax to get wrong, and the

Park UI (MIT) file-upload 102769c — recipe translated to Tailwind for @acaprino/sigrid (https://github.com/chakra-ui/park-ui/blob/102769c/packages/preset/src/recipes/file-upload.ts)

A zone that takes a file: dropped on it, or chosen with the system picker, so dragging is never the only way (WCAG
2.5.7). The look is the attachments zone's (Park's `file-upload` recipe): the raised sheet with l3 corners and a 2px
dashed border in the control colour that turns solid ink while a file is dragged over it (the accent is not for this,
R2), two lines of text and no upload icon (the words say it, R6), 96px tall so it is an easy target with a mouse and a
finger. Ark UI's FileUpload gives the real button that opens the picker, the input behind it (outside the
accessibility tree and the tab order, emptied before each choice so the same file can be chosen again) and the checks
of type, size and count; the drop is the toolkit's `useDropTarget` (a drag that starts in the page is left alone).
The words are the app's: the label (the button's name, the same while dragging or busy), the hint (its description),
the line while dragging and while busy, and the error under the zone. Busy, the button keeps its focus and ignores
clicks and drops, like a loading Button. No animation.

From Park's `field` recipe comes the form: a column with a 6px gap, the label in 14px medium ink, and the mark of a
required field after the label. Ours (the owner's design of 2026-11-22): the helper text is 12px muted, and the error
is a box on the soft destructive fill with the text in the destructive red, while the control keeps its border;
the required mark is the ink, not the accent (R2), and hidden from screen readers (the control says `required`).
The wiring is the toolkit's own, so any of its controls can sit inside (`Input`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `DateField`,
`ChipsInput`, `Switch`): the one child receives the `id` the label points to, `aria-describedby` with the helper or
the error, and `aria-invalid` when there is an error. The error is announced when it appears (`role="alert"`).
The headless `Field` of Base UI stays exported for an app that lays a field out by hand.

A one-line field with fixed parts inside it, before or after the text: words that are always there («https://»,
«.com», a unit), an icon, or a small button that acts on what is written (copy it, show it, empty it). The whole is
one field: one border, one height and one focus ring, around the parts and the text together (R4: no border inside
a border). It takes the props of `Input` and has its look, so a `FormField` wires it as it wires an `Input`:
the `id`, the note and the invalid state go to the `<input>`. A press on a part that is not a button puts the
caret in the field, as a press on the field would.
A button beside a field, with a border of its own («Subscribe» after an e-mail), is not this: it is an `Input` and
a `Button` in a `Cluster`.

A list of things to read and act on (messages, files, records): the content of the «list and detail» layout. Each
row has a title and, if the app has them, a second line under it, something before the title (an avatar, an icon), a
short fact at the end (a date, a size) and whatever else the caller adds there (a `Count`, a label).
It speaks the one language of every list of the toolkit:
- the row the user chose has the selection tint, stronger text and a short accent bar at its start (R1), and under
  the pointer a row takes a share of that tint;
- a row not read yet has a dot in the accent before its title and the title in semibold (R2: unread is one of the
  accent's places); the dot's slot stays when empty, so the titles line up;
- a row is one line as tall as the density's row, or two lines; with a finger it is at least 44px.
With `animated` the share of the tint under the pointer is one background for the whole list, which follows the
pointer from row to row (`HoverFollow`); the chosen row keeps its own tint over it, and the keyboard's focus ring
is the row's own, as without it.
The second line is a sentence (`description`), or short facts side by side (`facts`: a label with its dot, a project,
the day, a count of steps), which wrap rather than cut.
A row is a button, or a link with `href`, so nothing in it is a control: a button cannot hold a button. A thing one
both ticks and opens (a task, a file to clean) carries its one control beside the button (`control`, at the start or
the end): the list item is then the row, with the tint, the bar and the hover, and the control and the button are
two tab stops with their own names; a press on the control is the control's and never opens the row.
The rows of a navigation are `NavItem`: those are places, these are things.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Name of the list for screen readers («Messages»).

props.name: animated
props.doc: One hover background follows the pointer from row to row (off by default, never with prefers-reduced-motion).

props.name: title
props.doc: What the thing is: one line, cut with an ellipsis.

props.doc: The title takes up to two lines before it is cut: a list on a narrow screen, where a long name would lose its end.

props.name: description

props.name: meta

props.doc: This row is the one shown in the detail.

props.name: href
props.doc: With it the row is a link.

fields.name: color
fields.doc: A colour the person gave to it (a label's, a project's), one of the palette's: an 8px dot before the words (R10).

fields.name: numeric
fields.doc: Tabular figures: a count, a time.

The notes and the answers as Markdown blocks: paragraphs, lists, checkboxes (read-only), headings, quotes and fenced
blocks of code, with the inline marks inside (`InlineMarkdown`). It draws what `parseBlocks` reads
(`src/internal/markdown.tsx`): React elements only, never HTML, so a `<script>` written in a note stays text.
A fenced block («```ts») is a quiet box in the mono face, the language above it and a `CopyButton` beside it, always

text on the page (the answer is the content, not a bubble), with Markdown when it is a string. Each message says who

Park UI (MIT) alert 102769c — recipe translated to Tailwind for @acaprino/sigrid (https://github.com/chakra-ui/park-ui/blob/102769c/packages/preset/src/recipes/alert.ts)
A message that stays in the page until the app removes it: a failure, a warning, a success or a piece of
information, with a title, its text, an optional list and the actions that answer it. It has no close button: it
goes when its cause is gone. One need, one look: a failure the page shows is a note with `tone="error"` (with
«Retry» as its action when it can be tried again), never an `Empty`, which is only for a view with nothing in it; a
passing event (saved, moved, sent) is a toast (`Toasts`).
Each tone is said three ways, never by colour alone (DESIGN.md "Status"): its icon, from Sigrid's one set (`info`,
`check`, `alert` for a warning, `error` for a failure: the circle with an X that marks a failure everywhere, in a
toast, a progress and a step too), its colour, and a word read first by screen readers («Error: Could not reach the
server»: `useWords().common.error`, the word of an error toast, and `useWords().note` for the other three).
An error or a warning is announced when it appears (`role="alert"`, read at once), unless the app says `announce`
false: a warning that is a fact of the item shown (read only, out of date) would be read again at each selection.
Information and a success are not: they have no live role, so a screen reader meets them in the page's order. A
polite `role="status"` would not keep them quiet: some screen readers read a status as soon as it is put in the page,
and again at each change of its text. The root is keyed on its tone: a note whose tone changes in place is drawn
anew, so an information that becomes an error, or a warning that becomes an error, is announced as it appears.
A long word (a path, a JSON value, an address) breaks where it must (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`, inherited by the
title, the text and the list), so the note never grows wider than its place; a tool's output, with its line breaks,
goes in the text as a `<Text pre>`.
Form: Park's `alert` recipe, its default `subtle` variant at its `md` size: a row with the icon at the start and the
content beside it (12px apart, 16px of padding, l3 corners, 14px text), the title semibold over the text, 4px apart.
The fill is the tone's soft colour (the theme engine's `success-soft`, `warning-soft`, `destructive-soft`, as the
error box of `FormField`); information has no status colour and is never the accent (R2), so it is the quiet fill
(the ink at 6%). A fill and no border or shadow: it lies in the page, it is not raised (R4). The icon and the title
take the tone's colour, which reads on its soft fill in every theme; the text and the list stay in the ink.
Not taken from Park: its colour palettes (blue, orange, green, red: here the status tokens), the 20px icon (16px, R7),
the `solid`, `surface` and `outline` variants and the `lg` size (one form for every app). The actions are the
app's buttons, `outline` (the ink) or `ghost` (the soft ink), both at 4.5:1 on the four fills in every theme: a note
never holds the solid action unless it is the one of its screen (R3).

components.name: Note
components.doc: A message that stays in the page, in one of four tones, until the app removes it.

props.name: tone
props.doc: What kind of message it is: its icon, its colour and the word read before the title. `info` by default. An error or a warning is announced when it appears; a note whose tone changes is drawn anew, and announced if it is now one of them.

props.name: announce
props.doc: An error or a warning is announced when it appears (the default). `false` for one that is a fact of the item shown (a warning «Read only»), which would otherwise be read at each selection. Information and a success are never announced.

props.name: title
props.doc: What happened, in a few words («Could not reach the server»), without the tone's word: screen readers read it before the title. A long word breaks to fit.

props.name: children
props.doc: The text under the title: why, and what to do. A tool's output, with its line breaks, goes in a `<Text pre>`.

props.name: items
props.doc: A list under the text (the files that failed, the steps to take), one entry each; an empty list shows nothing.

props.name: actions
props.doc: The buttons that answer it («Retry», «Open the settings»), `outline` or `ghost`: the solid one only if it is the screen's one primary action (R3).

files.about:
One line of items (the details under a title, a row of labels) that never grows: what does not fit is cut from the
end, whole, and counted after the line («+2»). It never wraps to a second line and the first item always stays.
Other libraries call it an overflow list; this one is CSS and one `ResizeObserver`:
- the box is a flex row that wraps, one row tall, with `overflow: clip`: what does not fit wraps onto a row that is
  not shown. `clip` and not `hidden`: the box is no scroll container, so focus can never scroll the line.
- the items that sit below the first one are the cut ones. They are counted when the items are drawn, again when the
  box changes size, and again when the fonts are ready (a font that comes late changes the widths, not the box).
- a cut item is `inert` and invisible: no focus, no press, and screen readers skip it, as the eye does. So the cue is
  for both: «+2» to the eye, «2 more» to a screen reader (`words.list.more`). What is cut must also be found where
  the whole item is (its page, its details).
The caller gives the box its height in `className`: one row of its items (`h-5` for labels 20px tall), with the gap
and the text. Each child is one item: one element (a bare text is not counted: put it in a `<span>`). A first item
wider than the line is cut at the line's end: give it `min-w-0 truncate` for an ellipsis.
Its boxes are spans, so it also sits inside a button or a row's line. Without layout (jsdom, a server) nothing is
cut, and nothing moves.

props.name: children
props.doc: The items, in their order: one element each. What does not fit is cut from the end.

props.name: className
props.doc: Classes of the box that holds the items: its height (one row of the items, `h-5`), the gap, the text.

props.name: cue
props.doc: What stands after the line when items are cut, from how many they are. Default: «+2», read «2 more».

files.about:
What an assistant did on the way to its answer, kept behind a row each so the answer stays the thing to read:
`Reasoning`, what it thought, and `ToolCall`, a tool it used. Both are the toolkit's row that opens in place
(`Disclosure`): the same row, the same arrow, the same panel.
`Reasoning` is open while it is being written (`busy`) and closes by itself when it is done, unless the reader
opened or closed it: the reader's choice stays. Its row says «Thinking», then «Thought for 4 s». Its text is set
apart as a quote is: the soft ink behind a line at its start.
`ToolCall` says the tool's name and its state three ways, never by colour alone: an icon (a clock while it waits,
the bolt while it runs, a check, the circle with an X of a failure), its colour, and a word for screen readers. It
opens only when there is something to show: what the tool was given and what it gave back, as written, in the
monospace of code; a long one scrolls in its block, which the keyboard reaches.
Nothing loops: no shimmer and no spinner. A state changes once, when the app says so.

components.name: Reasoning
components.doc: The reasoning behind an answer, behind a row: open while it is written, closed once done.

props.name: busy
props.doc: It is being written: the row says so, and it is open unless the reader closed it.

props.name: seconds
props.doc: How long it took, in seconds, said by the row once it is done («Thought for 4 s»).

props.name: open
props.doc: Open or closed, when the app keeps it.

props.name: animated
props.doc: The arrow turns when the reader opens or closes the row. Absent: as `MotionProvider` says.

props.name: children
props.doc: The reasoning: a string is read as Markdown.

components.name: ToolCall
components.doc: A tool an assistant used: its name and its state, and behind the row what it was given and what it gave back.

props.name: name
props.doc: The tool's name, as the app calls it («Search the web», `read_file`).

props.name: status
props.doc: Where the call is. `success` by default. A value outside the four (from data) is `pending`.

props.name: summary
props.doc: A few words on what it did, after the name («3 results», the file's path): muted, cut when the row is short.

props.name: input
props.doc: What the tool was given. A string (JSON, a command) is shown as written, in a block that wraps.

props.name: output
props.doc: What it gave back, or why it failed. A string is shown as written.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Open at first. Default closed.

props.name: animated
props.doc: The arrow turns when the reader opens or closes the row. Absent: as `MotionProvider` says.

files.about:
A search box: the toolkit's `Input` as a `type="search"` field, with the magnifier at the start (functional chrome,
16px, muted) and, while there is text, a button at the end that empties the field and gives it the focus back. The
browser's own clear button is hidden, so there is one, with a name and the toolkit's focus ring. The field has no
label of its own: the caller names it (`aria-label`, or a `FormField` around it).
`variant="quiet"` is the same field for a bar (a header, a toolbar), where the search is always there and must not
weigh as much as the fields of the page: a well with round ends, a quiet fill in place of the border (`FIELD_QUIET`,
lib/field.ts), the light divider only under the pointer; in focus it is the page's ground with the focus ring of
every field. Its height, its text and its parts are the same; what tells it from the bar is the fill, and what says
it is a search is the magnifier and its words. The button that empties it is round as well.

props.name: value
props.doc: The text searched for.

props.name: clearLabel
props.doc: The name of the button that empties the field. Absent: the toolkit's words («Clear the search»).

props.name: variant
props.doc: `outline` (the default): the field of every form, with its border. `quiet`: for a search in a bar, a well with round ends, a quiet fill and no border at rest, so it does not stand out from the bar; the border shows under the pointer.

files.about:
A choice of a settings page (docs/patterns.md, «Sidebar and page»): its name, and a line under it if it needs one, at
the start; its control at the end (a `Switch`, a `ToggleGroup`, a `Select`); a hairline under it, so a page of them
reads as one list. The choice takes effect at once: no Save. A row that opens more (a page of its own, «Advanced»)
has no control: the whole row is the button, with a chevron at its end.
It is at least 48px tall, and 44px with a finger at any density. The control names itself (`aria-label` with the
row's name): the row only lays it out.

components.name: SettingRow
components.doc: One choice of a settings page: the name at the start, the control at the end.

props.name: label
props.doc: The name of the choice («Reminders»).

props.name: description
props.doc: A line under the name: what it does, what it is set to.

props.name: control
props.doc: The control at the end. Absent with `onClick`: the row opens more.

props.name: onClick
props.doc: The row is a button that opens more, with a chevron at its end, and holds no control.

files.about:
The steps of a task as a path (a signup, an import, a lesson, a pipeline): numbered dots joined by a line. It shows
what is done, where the user is and what is left, and the next step by its name: people finish when they know what
remains. Two facts are kept apart: what became of a step (`status`: done, running, to do, skipped, failed; without
it, what comes before `current` is done) and which step is on the screen (`current`). The accent is progress (R2):
a step done is a check on the accent tint, a running one a clock on it, the step on the screen is the one solid dot
(with its number, or the mark of its status: a done step looked at keeps its check), the steps to come and the
skipped ones (a dash) are a quiet fill, and the line is the accent after each step done. Round, as a dot may be (R7).
Nothing moves: the toolkit has no loop to reuse (a progress that does not know how far it is stands still too), so a
running step is told by its mark and its word («in progress», shown at the end of its row in a column).
With `onStepSelect` a step that is done, running, skipped or failed is a button that goes to it; one to come only when
the app gave it a `status` itself; a `disabled` one never, and it shows why (`reason`). In a column the whole row is
the target and takes the focus ring.
For screen readers it is an ordered list; the step on the screen has `aria-current="step"`, and each step says what
became of it (`words.steps`, in any language).
A step that failed has the one look of a failure: Sigrid's `error` icon (the circle with an X) in its dot, in red.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Name of the path for screen readers («Signup»).

props.name: current
props.doc: The step on the screen, counting from 0: it has `aria-current` and the one solid dot, whatever its status. Steps without a `status` are done before it and to come after it; `steps.length` means all are done, -1 that none is on the screen.

props.name: onStepSelect
props.doc: With it, each step that is done, running, skipped or failed is a button that goes to it; a step to come only when its `status` is given, and a `disabled` one never. In a column the whole row is the target.

props.name: orientation
props.doc: `vertical` (the default): a column, with the descriptions beside the dots. `horizontal`: a row; it measures its own width, so it needs one of its own (`w-full`, or a width), and in a place too narrow for the names it keeps the current one and says «Step 2 of 4».

fields.name: label
fields.doc: The name of the step («Account», «Choose a plan»): short, as it is the next thing the user reads.

fields.name: description
fields.doc: A line under the name, for the step the user is on or the one next: what it asks.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: What became of the step, whatever its place: `done`, `running` (a clock, and the words «in progress»), `todo`, `skipped` (a dash) or `error` (it failed: red, with Sigrid's `error` icon). Absent: the steps before `current` are done and the others are to come.

fields.name: meta
fields.doc: A short fact at the end of the row («2 min», «3 of 6»), in figures of one width. In a column only.

fields.name: disabled
fields.doc: The step cannot be gone to yet: it is never a button. Say why in `reason`.

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: Why a `disabled` step cannot be gone to yet («Run the analysis first»): shown under its name, so read by everyone.

files.about:
A row of ready-made requests, for a conversation that has not started or an answer that can be followed up: quiet
chips (the neutral fill, never the accent: R2), which wrap to more lines when the row is short. Choosing one tells
the app, which usually puts its text in the `PromptInput` for the user to send or change, rather than sending it at
once: a suggestion is a start, not a commitment.

components.name: Suggestions
components.doc: A row of quiet chips, one per ready-made request. An empty list shows nothing.

props.name: label
props.doc: The name of the row for screen readers. Absent: the toolkit's word («Suggestions»).

props.name: animated
props.doc: A chip answers the press with a movement. Absent: as `MotionProvider` says.

types.name: Suggestion
types.doc: One ready-made request.

fields.name: label
fields.doc: What the chip says, and usually the text put in the field.

fields.name: icon
fields.doc: An icon that tells what kind of request it is; none for most.

files.about:
A choice among the user's colours: the toolkit's radio group of swatches, each named by its colour (the words' names,
or «Color 8» for one that has none, never the hexadecimal).

components.name: Swatches
components.doc: Color choice for what the user colours (a folder, a group): the SmoothUI/Base UI RadioGroup (`primitives/radio-group`) with solid swatches. Like any radio group: a single Tab stop (the chosen color, or the first), the arrows move and choose wrapping around the ends, Home and End go to the first and the last.

files.about:
SmoothUI (MIT) toast 4.0.0 — adapted for @acaprino/sigrid (https://smoothui.dev/r/base-nova/toast.json)
Park UI (MIT) toast 102769c — recipe translated to Tailwind for @acaprino/sigrid (https://github.com/chakra-ui/park-ui/blob/102769c/packages/preset/src/recipes/toast.ts)

From SmoothUI the surface of a notice is left: the dark card (the ink, with the paper as its text, as in the approved
preview), with the text, the action and the close button on one row, the quick choices on a second one. Park's
toast recipe is a light surface card: of it we take the form (l3 corners, the lg elevation, 16px of side padding, the
action in semibold) and the keys as outline keys, not its colors. Everything it does rests on Ark UI's Toast (`@ark-ui/react/toast`): a
toaster store, the `Toaster` region and one toast machine per notice (its time, its leaving). What Ark gives and what
stays ours:
- Ark: the region (Alt+T moves focus to it, Ark's own key; in an `AppShell` F6 reaches it in the round of the frame), the life of a notice (its timer, the "dismissing" phase that keeps it in
  the DOM while it leaves, `removeDelay`), the root and title parts, and the region as a branch of Ark's dismissable
  layers (a click on a notice is not "outside" an Ark popover).
- Ours: the list is the caller's (`items`); an effect carries it into the store (adds the new ones, closes the removed
  ones). The column: at most `COLUMN_MAX` notices one above the other, all readable, the newest at the bottom; one
  more pushes the oldest out from the top (Ark's `max` would keep the new one waiting instead) and the others move
  up one place. Ark's own layouts are not used (`overlap` off): its places follow its own list, which still holds a
  notice while it leaves, so the others would wait for it to be gone before closing the gap.
- the region is `role="status"` with `aria-relevant="additions"` and a name in English; a notice is not a `status`
  with `tabIndex=0` of its own: no extra Tab stop per notice;
- the time is Ark's, but it starts over: while the pointer is on the column or focus is inside it no notice counts
  down (`duration` Infinity), and when it is left each one is rearmed from the start;
- Esc does not close a notice on its own: only `durationMs` (which calls `onDismiss`), a notice past `COLUMN_MAX` or the caller.
Motion: with `animated` the notices move with the list transition (`NOTICES` in `motion-impl`); without it, or with
prefers-reduced-motion, the same places are plain styles and nothing moves.

components.name: Toasts
components.doc: The notices: a column at the bottom right (in the middle on the phone), read by screen readers without interrupting. At most `max` (ten by default), one above the other, the newest at the bottom; one more pushes the oldest out from the top. With `durationMs` and `onDismiss` each notice shows the seconds left and a «×» to close it at once.

props.name: items
props.doc: The notices, oldest first. The column shows the `max` newest: one more pushes the oldest out (and calls `onDismiss`).

props.name: max
props.doc: How many the column holds, up to `COLUMN_MAX` (ten, R12 of the toolkit's rules, 2026-11-20).

props.name: inline
props.doc: In the page flow instead of fixed at the bottom: for documentation and previews.

props.name: durationMs
props.doc: After how many milliseconds a notice calls `onDismiss`. Without it (or without `onDismiss`) the notices stay until the caller removes them, as before. With the pointer on the column or focus inside it the time is suspended; when it is left the time starts over.

props.name: onDismiss
props.doc: Called once per notice when `durationMs` runs out, or when newer notices push it out of the column: the caller removes it from `items`.

props.name: animated
props.doc: The column moves: a notice enters and leaves, the others slide into place (off by default, never with prefers-reduced-motion).

types.name: ToastAction
types.doc: An extra action on a notice (a quick choice after a gesture): `pressed` marks it as already chosen.

fields.name: undo
fields.type: { label?: string; hint?: string | undefined; onClick: () => void; }
fields.doc: «Undo». `hint` is the key that does the same thing right now (for example «Z»): it is shown next to the button.

fields.name: actions
fields.doc: Quick choices, on a second row: groups of buttons (each group has a name for screen readers).

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: `error`: something failed and the user has to know. It never counts down (`durationMs` does not apply to it), it shows no seconds, and newer notices push the others out before it: it stays until it is closed (the «×», with `onDismiss`) or the caller removes it. A mark before the text says what it is (Sigrid's `error` icon, the one look of a failure), and screen readers hear «Error». A failure the page shows until its cause is gone is a `Note` with `tone="error"`, not a toast.

files.about:
A small Markdown of our own, for a title and the notes under it. No dependencies and no `innerHTML`: the text becomes
React elements, so a `<script>` written in a note stays text. Links are not opened from here (the app that uses the
package does it): they are shown underlined, with the address as a hint.

Inline (title and notes): **bold** or __bold__, *italic* or _italic_, ~~strikethrough~~, `code`, [text](url).
In blocks (notes only): lines starting with «- », «* » or «1. » (lists), «- [ ] » and «- [x] » (checkboxes, read-only),
«# » (heading), «> » (quote), a fenced block of code («```lang» to «```», or «~~~»; unclosed it runs to the end, so a
text still arriving shows as code from its first line); an empty line separates paragraphs. A «\*» stays an asterisk.
The parser is here; `MarkdownBlocks` (`src/components/markdown-blocks.tsx`) draws the blocks.

components.name: InlineMarkdown
components.doc: An inline line (the title): bold, italic, strikethrough, code, link. No blocks.

files.about:
The frame around, for the parts that change with it: `AppShell` (src/layout/app-shell.tsx) gives it, and what is
below the frame reads it without importing the frame (a `Page`, a primitive, keeps the frame's margins only inside
one). The frame hands both out again under the same names.

fields.name: sidebar
fields.doc: `full`: the user's choice holds. `rail`: forced to its icons. `drawer`: out of the layout, opened over the page.

fields.name: inspector
fields.doc: `docked` beside the content, or a `drawer` over its end.

files.about:
The frame of an app: one layout with seven regions, after Imago's `im-shell`, so every app of the suite is laid out
alike and an app fills in only the regions it needs.

  ┌ title bar: app · views · toolbar · window buttons ───────┐
  ├ tabs: the views, when they are not in the bar ───────────┤
  ├ status: the last result · a summary ────────────────────┤
  │ sidebar │ content                    │ inspector         │
  │         ├ actions: the primary one at the end ───────────┤
  ├─────────┴ footer: service · counts · keys ───────────────┤
  └ bottom bar: the views, when they are at the foot ────────┘

The frame measures its own width, not the screen's, so a window half-snapped on a wide screen is laid out as the
narrow window it is. Three steps, Imago's:
- 1000px or more: the inspector is docked at the end and pushes the content; under it, it covers the end of the
  content as a panel with no backdrop (the page beside it keeps working);
- 850px or more: the sidebar is whole, or a rail if the user shrank it; from 620px to 850px it is the rail, whatever
  the user chose; under 620px it is out of the layout and opens as a drawer from a button of the title bar.
The steps are a recommendation, not a rule: an app with a narrower sidebar or a wider inspector passes its own
(`steps`), and a step set to 0 never happens (`steps={{ rail: 0, sidebar: 0 }}` keeps the sidebar whole at any width).
With `desktop` the frame is the window of a program and not a page (what Imago's windows do):
- its chrome is not selectable and keeps the arrow cursor, as in any program; the content, the body of the
  inspector, every field and whatever carries `data-selectable` stay selectable (theme.css);
- what opens over the window (dialogs, sheets, menus, the command palette) opens under the title bar and not over
  it, so the window can still be moved, minimized and closed while a dialog is open: the overlays of the frame mount
  into a layer that starts under the bar.
The keys and menus of the browser engine are a separate switch, `useDesktopGuard`, since a page in a tab keeps them.
Two forms, chosen with `frame`, with the same regions and steps:
- `line` (the default): one surface, the page, with a line between the regions;
- `sheet` (Xiox's frame, Imago's Smooth look; its glass is a theme's `material`): the title bar and the sidebar sit on the window's
  ground with no line and no fill of their own, and the work area (status, content, inspector, actions, footer) is
  one sheet of the page's surface with a line at its top and, where a sidebar lies beside it, at its start, with the
  large corner there. The ground is the sidebar's surface, so a light sidebar and the ground are one; a theme with a
  sidebar of its own colours (`data-sidebar="own"`, a dark or solid column) keeps its column on the lanes' surface.
  Where the sidebar is a drawer (under 620px) the sheet reaches the window's edge and has no corner.
The `Sidebar` and the `Inspector` read the step from the frame (`useAppShell`), so the app passes them as they are.
F6 moves the focus to the next region (title bar, sidebar, content, inspector, the notices) and Shift+F6 to the one
before, round again, skipping a region that is absent, closed or has nothing to focus: always, with nothing for the
app to write (after Imago's `regions`). The frame answers F6 before anything else does (the notices' own F6 among
them), so the round is one. In a region the focus goes to the place the user is in (`aria-current`), else to the first
thing that takes it; the content takes it itself when it holds nothing that does.
The inspector leaves the rest of the window working, in both forms: a press outside it does not close it (a row, a
node of a canvas, the search field are still the person's), opening it does not move the focus, and closing it gives
the focus back only when the focus was in it: to what last had it outside, or to the content when that is gone.
Its button closes it, and so does Escape with the focus in it, in both forms (not on a field that holds text or on
an open list or menu, whose key it is); as a drawer a swipe towards its edge does too. Escape with the focus
elsewhere is not the inspector's: it goes to what has the focus and to the app's commands.
Without a way to measure (a server, a test) the frame is the wide one.
Its height is the host's, never a guess (docs/mobile.md, «Heights and orientation»):
- it is as tall as what the person sees (`--app-height`, which it keeps up to date itself with `useAppHeight`: the
  browser's bars, the keyboard, a rotation), and never taller than the box it is put in, so a frame in a box of the
  app's keeps to the box (in a box taller than the window, `className="h-full"` makes it fill the box); the app adds
  no `h-dvh`;
- where it is the whole screen (as tall as what is seen: `data-screen`), it keeps clear of the device's edges (the
  notch, the status bar, the gesture bar: `env(safe-area-inset-*)`, the foot with its maximum, which does not change
  while the page scrolls), and it writes how much it keeps at its foot (the actions, the footer, the bottom bar) to
  `--bottom-bar-room` on the root, so the notices sit above it;
- under 500px of height (`short:`, a phone lying down) the bottom bar is 44px and its views put the word beside the
  icon, so the bar does not eat the screen.

props.name: titleBar
props.doc: The bar at the top (a `TitleBar`).

props.name: tabs
props.doc: Directly under the bar, across the whole window: the views of the app (a `Toolbar` of `ToolbarTabs`), when they are not in the bar.

props.name: status
props.doc: Under the bar: the last result and a summary, one line.

props.name: sidebar
props.doc: The navigation (a `Sidebar`).

props.name: inspector
props.doc: The details of what is selected (an `Inspector`).

props.name: actions
props.doc: Under the content: the actions on it, the primary one last (R3: one).

props.name: footer
props.doc: The foot: the state of the service, counts, the keys that work now.

props.name: bottomBar
props.doc: Under everything, across the whole window: the views of the app as tabs at the foot (a `Toolbar` of `ToolbarTabs` with `edge="top"`). Where the frame is the whole screen it keeps clear of the gesture bar, and its height (with the actions and the footer above it) is written to `--bottom-bar-room`.

props.name: desktop
props.doc: The frame is the window of a program: chrome that is not selectable, and overlays that open under the title bar. Leave it off for a page in a browser tab.

props.name: frame
props.doc: `line` (the default): one surface with lines between the regions. `sheet`: the title bar and the sidebar on the window's ground, the work area one sheet with a corner, as in Xiox.

props.name: steps
props.doc: The app's own steps, all or some, in place of the recommended ones (`APP_SHELL_STEPS`); 0 switches a step off.

props.name: contentLabel
props.doc: The name of the content for screen readers, and where the skip link goes.

props.name: children
props.doc: The content: what the app is for. It scrolls by itself.

components.name: Inspector
components.doc: The details or the form of what is selected, at the end of the frame. It is not modal: the rest of the window keeps working beside it. Docked it is a column with a line at its inner edge (R4); in a frame under 1000px it is a raised panel over the end of the content. Closed, the content takes its room. A press outside it does not close it, and opening it does not move the focus (a selection opened it, not a request: the person goes in with Tab, F6 or a press). Closed with the focus in it, it gives the focus back to what last had it outside, or to the content when that is gone or hidden; closed with the focus elsewhere, it moves nothing. It does the same when it is taken out of the page while open. When what had the focus in it is removed, the focus stays in it, on the inspector itself (it takes the focus, with the ring of a region: F6 lands there too when it holds no control).

props.name: title
props.doc: What it shows («Details»): its heading and its name for screen readers.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.doc: With it, a button in the heading closes the inspector, and so does Escape pressed with the focus in it (not on a field that holds text, nor on an open list or menu); as a drawer a swipe towards its edge does too. A press outside it never closes it, and Escape with the focus elsewhere is left to the app (a command on Escape).

props.name: footer
props.doc: Under the body, always in sight: the actions on what is selected.

props.name: animated
props.doc: The drawer slides in (off by default, never with prefers-reduced-motion).

files.about:
Two panes in the content region: a column of fixed width at the start with the list the thing is chosen from, and
beside it the thing chosen, read or worked on in the room that is left (a mail client's messages and the message, a
file browser's tree and the file). The frame's inspector is for the details or the form of what is selected, in
300px; this is for when the thing chosen is the work itself and needs the width.
- Each pane scrolls by itself; a hairline at the column's inner edge parts them (R4: a line, not a box).
- It measures its own width, as the frame does, never the screen's: with less room than the column and as much
  again for the other pane (`step`, by default twice the column), one pane is on screen at a time, the one `show`
  names. The other stays in the page, hidden, so the way back finds the list as it was left. The app is told when
  the form changes (`onPanesChange`): with one pane it shows its own way back to the list (a «back» button in the bar).
- Without a way to measure (a server, a test) it has its two panes, as the frame is the wide one.
The column's widths are steps of the scale: `sm` 240px, `md` 320px, `lg` 360px (a column of messages with a line of
each under the sender).

components.name: ContentSplit
components.doc: A column of fixed width with a list, and the thing chosen beside it; one at a time where the two do not fit.

props.name: aside
props.doc: The column at the start: the list the thing is chosen from.

props.name: asideLabel
props.doc: The column's name for screen readers («Messages», «Files»): it is a region of its own.

props.name: width
props.doc: The column's width: `sm` 240px, `md` 320px (the default), `lg` 360px.

props.name: show
props.doc: The pane on screen when only one fits: the column (`aside`, the default) or the thing chosen (`main`).

props.name: step
props.doc: The width of the split, in px, under which one pane shows at a time. Absent: twice the column's width. 0: always two.

props.name: onPanesChange
props.doc: The form changed: 2 panes side by side, or 1 at a time. Told once at first, when the split has measured itself.

props.name: children
props.doc: The other pane: the thing chosen, in the room that is left.

files.about:
The button in the bar that opens the sidebar, where the frame has taken the sidebar out of the layout and made it a
drawer (`useAppShell().sidebar === 'drawer'`, under 620px of the frame's width): on a wider frame the sidebar is in
sight, and the button is not drawn (docs/patterns.md, «Start from the one frame»). It is a `ToolbarButton`, an icon
with its name as a hint, the first thing of the bar; the app keeps the drawer's state and passes it to `Sidebar open`.

components.name: DrawerButton
components.doc: Opens the sidebar where it is a drawer; elsewhere it is not there.

props.name: onOpen
props.doc: Opens the drawer: the app sets the `open` it passes to its `Sidebar`.

props.name: label
props.doc: Its name, and its hint. Absent: the toolkit's words («Open the menu»).

props.name: animated
props.doc: The hint fades in (off by default, never with prefers-reduced-motion).

files.about:
The rows of a navigation (R1 and R6 of the owner's rules): a list of places, each a row with an icon slot, a name
and, at the end, whatever the caller adds (a `Count`). The row of the place the user is in carries
`aria-current="page"`, the selection tint, stronger text and a short accent bar at its left edge (R1). The icon slot is always there,
16px wide, so a row without an icon stays aligned with the others (R6). A row is as tall as the density's row, and
at least 44px with a coarse pointer.
A row may have a second line under its name (`description`) and, beside it, controls of its own (`actions`: a button
that adds to the place, a menu). The controls sit outside the row, which is itself a button or a link; the rail shows
neither.
Two tones: `page` (the default) for a list on the page or on a raised sheet, `sidebar` for a list on the app's
sidebar, where the theme has its own ink and its own selection (`sidebar-*`, the solid sidebar among them).
With motion on (`animated` on the `NavList` or the `Sidebar`, or `MotionProvider`) the tint and the bar of the chosen
row are one mark for the whole navigation, which slides from the row the user left to the row they chose, as the
tint of `Tabs` does (`Highlight` in `motion-impl`): one place is current, so there is one mark, and it crosses the
groups. It moves only when the current row changes; a row that is not shown (a closed group, a search) has no mark,
so the mark never comes from, or goes to, a place that is not seen.

props.name: current
props.doc: This row is the place the user is in.

props.name: icon
props.doc: The icon (an `Icon`): without one the slot stays, empty.

props.name: end
props.doc: What follows the name, at the end of the row: a `Count`.

props.name: description
props.doc: A second line under the name, in the muted ink: what the place holds, its state («4 sessions · 4 running»). Not on the rail.

props.name: actions
props.doc: Controls of the place (a button that adds to it, a menu), beside the row and outside it: the row is itself a button or a link. Not on the rail.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Name of the navigation for screen readers («Mail folders»).

props.name: animated
props.doc: The tint of the chosen row slides to the row chosen next (off by default, never with prefers-reduced-motion).

files.about:
A panel: the inner layout of a region of the frame (the content, the inspector), as Imago's `im-panel` and Xiox's
list are laid out. A header with the title, a line beside it that says how much is there («70 items · 8 selected»)
and the tools of the whole panel at its end (a filter, a switch); under it a row of tools (a search, «Fold all»);
then the body, which alone scrolls; and a foot that stays in sight (the actions on what is in the panel). With tools
at the end of the header, the row of tools keeps 8px from them.
Every part is optional but the title. The panel paints nothing: it lies on the surface of the region that holds it
(the page, or the sheet of `AppShell frame="sheet"`), and only the foot has a line above it (R4). It is a region
named by its title, so a screen reader can jump to it.

components.name: Panel
components.doc: A titled region with a header, a row of tools, a body that scrolls and a foot that stays.

props.name: title
props.doc: The name of the panel: its heading and the name of its region.

props.name: subtitle
props.doc: Beside the title, quieter: how much is there, what is chosen.

props.name: actions
props.doc: At the end of the header: the tools of the whole panel (a filter, a switch).

props.name: tools
props.doc: A row under the header: a search, a «Fold all».

props.name: footer
props.doc: Under the body, always in sight: the actions on what the panel holds, the primary one last.

props.name: level
props.doc: The level of the heading: 2 (the default), or 3 for a panel inside a region that has its own heading.

props.name: children
props.doc: The body: it scrolls by itself.

files.about:
A line of the sidebar that is not a place: what sits in its `header` or its `footer`, as the account (an avatar and a
name) or a switch of what the rows show (a check box and its words). It lines up with the rows of the navigation
(their padding, at every density) and keeps their height, 44px with a finger; its words take the sidebar's ink and
are cut with an ellipsis; the actions on the whole sidebar (a new folder, close all) sit at its end. It is not a
button: what can be pressed in it is the controls it holds.

components.name: SidebarRow
components.doc: A row of the sidebar's head or foot: the account, a switch of the view, the name of the list with its actions.

props.name: leading
props.doc: Before the words: an avatar, a check box, an icon.

props.name: end
props.doc: At the end: the actions on the whole sidebar, small quiet buttons with their name.

props.name: children
props.doc: The words, on one line.

files.about:
The sidebar of an app: its navigation as groups of rows (`NavItem`), on the theme's sidebar surface and inks
(`sidebar-*`). It puts together pieces the toolkit already has, so an app does not assemble them by hand:
- shrunk to a rail (`collapsed`) each row shows its icon alone, with its name as a hint beside it and still as its
  name for screen readers; the button at the foot shrinks and widens it (`onCollapsedChange`), or, with
  `toggle="head"`, the button at the end of the header's row (the name of the list, its count and the button on one
  row; on the rail the button alone, at the top);
- groups (`SidebarGroup`): a heading with its icon (R6) and, if `collapsible`, an arrow that turns as the group opens;
  the rows a user reaches most are simply the first group («Favorites»);
- a search box at the top (`search`) hides, as the user types, the rows whose name does not hold the text, and the
  groups left with no row; with nothing left it says so;
- below 860px (the `md` of theme.css, where the sidebar stops being a column) it is a drawer from the left, a `Sheet`
  the app opens from its own button (`open`, `onOpenChange`); choosing a row closes it.
Inside an `AppShell` the steps are the frame's (`app-shell.tsx`): a rail the width forces has no button to widen it.
What sits above the groups (the app's name, a menu that changes workspace) and below them (the account) is the app's:
`header` and `footer`. No rail or bar marks the current row: the selection tint does (R1).
With `animated` that tint is one mark for the whole sidebar, which slides to the row chosen next, across the groups
(`NavItem`, nav-list.tsx). It is drawn anew, without a slide, when the sidebar shrinks to its rail or widens, and a
row in a closed group or hidden by the search has none.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Name of the navigation for screen readers («Main»); also the title of the drawer.

props.name: collapsed
props.doc: Shrunk to a rail of icons. On a narrow window (the drawer) it is always wide.

props.name: onCollapsedChange
props.doc: With it, a button at the foot shrinks and widens the sidebar.

props.name: toggle
props.doc: Where that button is. `foot` (the default): alone at the foot, under the groups. `head`: at the end of the header's row, beside `header` (a `SidebarRow` with the name of the list and its `Count`); with no `header` the row holds the button alone; on the rail it is at the top, centred. Where there is no button (no `onCollapsedChange`, the drawer, a rail the frame's width forces) it changes nothing.

props.name: open
props.doc: Where the sidebar is a drawer, the drawer is open: inside an `AppShell` under 620px of frame, alone under 860px of screen. Where it is a column or a rail, it is always there and this is not read.

props.name: header
props.doc: Above the groups: the app's name, a menu that changes workspace. On the rail it is not shown.

props.name: footer
props.doc: Below the groups: the account, a link to the settings. On the rail it is not shown.

props.name: search
props.doc: A search box at the top that filters the rows as the user types.

props.name: animated
props.doc: The drawer slides in, the arrows of the groups turn and the tint of the chosen row slides to the row chosen next (off by default, never with prefers-reduced-motion).

components.name: SidebarGroup
components.doc: A group of rows of the sidebar. On the rail the heading is not shown and every group is open, so no icon is hidden; while a search is on every group is open too, and one with no row left is hidden.

props.name: label
props.doc: The heading of the group («Favorites», «Projects»). Without it the rows stand alone, as the first group often does.

props.name: icon
props.doc: The icon of the heading (an `Icon`), R6: without one the slot stays, empty.

props.name: collapsible
props.doc: The heading opens and closes the group.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: A group that opens and closes: open at first (the default) or closed.

files.about:
Two panes side by side with a divider the person moves: the list and the thing read beside it, where each wants the
width the person gives it (a session list and its transcript, a file tree and a file). `ContentSplit` is the fixed
column; this is the one whose column moves.
- The divider is a window splitter: one tab stop, `role="separator"` with its value in px between the two minimums.
  A pointer drags it (the pane follows while it moves, and the size is kept when the pointer is let go). The arrows
  move it 16px (Shift, 64px; the end the arrow points to), Home takes the first pane to its minimum and End to its
  largest, a double press puts it back to the size it started with. In a language written from the right the arrows
  and the drag follow the panes.
- Each pane keeps `minStart` and `minEnd` px. A split narrower than the two minimums and the divider shows one pane
  at a time, the one `show` names, as `ContentSplit` does; the other stays in the page, hidden, and the app is told of
  the form (`onPanesChange`) to put its way back in the bar.
- The size is the person's, and the app can keep it: `size` and `onSizeChange` (null: put back to the default), or
  just a `storageKey`, under which the size is kept in the browser's storage (a store that fails keeps nothing, and
  the split works the same).
- It measures its own width, as the frame does, never the screen's. Without a way to measure (a server, a test) it
  has its two panes and keeps the size as it is.
A hairline at the divider (R4: a line, not a box); the divider is wider where a finger is the pointer.

components.name: SplitPane
components.doc: Two panes with a divider that moves with the pointer and the keys, the size kept where the app says.

props.name: start
props.doc: The pane at the start: the list.

props.name: startLabel
props.doc: The start pane's name for screen readers («Sessions»): it is a region of its own.

props.name: endLabel
props.doc: The other pane's name for screen readers («Transcript»).

props.name: label
props.doc: The divider's name for screen readers («Resize the sessions list»); its hint says how to move it.

props.name: size
props.doc: The width of the start pane, in px, when the app keeps it; `null` is the default width. With it, the size is the app's: pass what `onSizeChange` gives.

props.name: defaultSize
props.doc: The width at first, and the one a double press puts back, in px. Default 320.

props.name: onSizeChange
props.doc: The person moved the divider (a drag is told once, when it ends) or put it back (`null`).

props.name: storageKey
props.doc: Where the browser keeps the size, when the app does not (`size`): a name of the app's («mukade.split.sessions»).

props.name: minStart
props.doc: The least width of the start pane, in px. Default 180.

props.name: minEnd
props.doc: The least width of the end pane, in px. Default 240.

props.name: show
props.doc: The pane on screen when only one fits: the start pane (the default) or the end pane (`end`).

props.name: onPanesChange
props.doc: The form changed: 2 panes side by side, or 1 at a time. Told once at first, when the split has measured itself.

props.name: children
props.doc: The end pane: the thing read, in the room that is left.

files.about:
The bar at the top of a window: the place of its name and of its toolbar, on the same row as the buttons that
minimize, maximize and close it. It is plain web: on a page in a browser it is the app's top bar and nothing else.
What makes it the frame of a window is given from outside, so the toolkit knows no window API:
- the empty parts of the bar move the window. The standard way is the `app-region` property, set in theme.css on the
  bar and taken off every control inside it; a host that marks its drag regions with an attribute of its own gets it
  through `dragProps`, which the bar, the toolbar inside it, its title and its spacers all carry (such a mark often
  counts only on the element under the pointer);
- the room the system keeps for its own buttons over the page (the window-controls overlay of an installed web app)
  is left free: theme.css reads it into `--titlebar-start` and `--titlebar-end`, and an app can set the two itself;
- where the system draws no buttons, `WindowControls` draws them and calls the app back; the app talks to its host.
  On Windows 11 a host can lay the system's own hit area over the maximize button, so the Snap Layouts open from it:
  the pointer then never reaches the page's button. `maximizeRef` gives the host the button to measure, and
  `maximizeState` shows on it the hover and the press the system reports (Imago's window does this).
The bar is as tall as a dense control and 8px above and below it (`--titlebar-height`), on the page's own surface
with a line under it (R4: a line, no shadow). With `size="compact"` it is the thin caption of a classic desktop
program: the smallest control and 2px above and below it (32px at normal density), and the toolbar inside it takes
the small size by itself. Nothing else changes: it is a measure, chosen with a parameter.

props.name: size
props.doc: `compact`: the thin caption of a classic desktop program, with small controls.

props.name: dragProps
props.doc: The host's own mark of a drag region, if it has one.

props.name: windowControls
props.doc: The window's buttons (`WindowControls`), at the end of the bar and flush with its corner.

components.name: WindowControls
components.doc: The three buttons of a window, for a host that draws none: as tall as the bar, 44px wide, with no gap. The last one takes the accent under the pointer, as in Imago: closing a window destroys nothing, and red is kept for danger. They only call back: what minimizes, maximizes and closes the window is the app's.

props.name: maximized
props.doc: The window fills the screen: the middle button restores it.

props.name: onMinimize
props.doc: Each button is drawn only if its action is given.

props.name: maximizeRef
props.doc: The middle button, for a host that needs its rectangle.

props.name: maximizeState
props.doc: The pointer over the middle button as the system sees it, when the system and not the page receives it.

files.about:
The toolbar: one row of actions that is a single Tab stop. Base UI's `Toolbar` carries the behaviour (the arrows
move among the items, Home and End reach the ends, a disabled item stays reachable); the form is the toolkit's
`Button` recipe at the dense height, so an item is the same control as everywhere else.
- `ToolbarButton` is an action. With no children it is an icon alone: its `label` is its accessible name and the
  hint under the pointer (with the `shortcut` after it, as plain text: R5). With children it is an icon and a word.
  `pressed` makes it a switch (a filter that is on, a panel that is open): the selection tint, never the accent fill.
  One item of a toolbar may be `variant="default"`, the one solid action of the screen (R3); the rest stay quiet.
- `ToolbarSearch` is a search box that takes no room until it is asked for: a magnifier that opens into the
  toolkit's `SearchField` on a press (or when the app opens it from its own key), and closes again with Esc, or when
  it is left empty. While it holds text it stays open, so what filters the page is always in sight.
- `ToolbarBrand` is the app at the start of the bar, as in Imago's apps: a small square in the accent holding the
  initial of the product's name, and the name beside it, or the name alone (`mark={false}`). With `page` the place
  follows the name after a chevron («Daodan › Settings»). No drawn logo: the hue and the name tell the apps apart.
- `ToolbarTabs` are the views of the app as words in the bar, after the brand, as in Xiox («Cleanup · Registry ·
  Developers · Settings»): the view the user is in has the stronger text and a short bar in the accent under it. The
  same tabs can sit in a toolbar of their own directly under the title bar (`AppShell`'s `tabs`), in a bar at the
  foot of the window (`bottomBar`, with `edge="top"` and, on a narrow window, `layout="stacked"`: the icon over the
  word), or small in the status bar (`size="sm"` in the `footer`).
- A button with a word shows its `shortcut` after the word, as plain text («Commands Ctrl K»): the way into the
  command palette.
- `ToolbarSeparator`, `ToolbarGroup`, `ToolbarTitle` and `ToolbarSpacer` lay the row out. Inside a `TitleBar` the
  root, the title and the spacers also carry the bar's drag attributes, so the empty parts of the bar move the window.
Short of room the bar gives way in fixed steps, measured on the toolbar itself and not on the screen (a container
query, as Imago's frame does: a window half-snapped is narrow on a wide screen). Under 448px a button with an icon
and a word keeps the icon alone, and the search shown as a field is its magnifier; under 256px the title goes.
What the user needs to act (the buttons) is never what gives way.
The tools keep their places from one page or state to the next (the owner's rule, above all on a phone): a tool that
a view lacks keeps its place, empty (`absent`), and a view's word is as wide chosen as not. What grows (a search that
opens, the place in the brand) sits next to a `ToolbarSpacer`, so it takes the spacer's room and not a tool's place.
Two sizes, chosen with a parameter: `md`, and `sm` for the dense bars of a classic desktop program (28px items, a
20px mark). A toolbar in a compact `TitleBar` is `sm` by itself. Text buttons that open a `DropdownMenu` («File»,
«Edit», «View») make the menu bar of such a program out of the same parts.
Icons are the app's (an `Icon`, or any 16px drawing); the magnifier is functional chrome, as in `SearchField`.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Name of the toolbar for screen readers («Message actions»).

props.name: size
props.doc: `md` (the default): 32px items at normal density. `sm`: 28px items, for the dense bars of a classic desktop program. Absent: `sm` in a compact `TitleBar`, `md` elsewhere.

components.name: ToolbarBrand
components.doc: The app, at the start of the bar: the mark and the name. In a `TitleBar` both move the window. Under 256px of toolbar the name goes and the mark stays.

props.name: name
props.doc: The name of the product («Xiox»): shown beside the mark, and the source of its letter.

props.name: mark
props.doc: In place of the letter, the app's own mark (a 16px drawing): the square stays. `false`: the name alone.

props.name: page
props.doc: Where the user is, after the name: «Daodan › Settings». One name, or the path to it. On a toolbar under 448px the app's name gives way and the place stays, after the mark.

props.name: label
props.doc: The name of the action: the accessible name, and the hint of a button that shows an icon alone.

props.name: icon
props.doc: The drawing, 16px (an `Icon`).

props.name: shortcut
props.doc: The key that does the same («Ctrl K»): plain text in the hint.

props.name: variant
props.doc: `ghost` (the default) for an action among others, `outline` for one that stands out, `default` for the one solid action (R3). `quiet` is an outline that does not ask to be pressed (the way to the commands, with its key): the hairline of a divider and the muted ink, the ink under the pointer; it keeps the hairline under a theme with strong control borders (`ThemeDef.controls`), where an `outline` takes the control border.

props.name: pressed
props.doc: A switch: on or off. Absent: a plain action.

props.name: keepWord
props.doc: With an icon and a word: the word stays on a narrow bar too (by default it gives way under 448px).

props.name: animated
props.doc: The hint fades in (off by default, never with prefers-reduced-motion).

props.name: absent
props.doc: The tool is not there in this view or this state: its place stays, empty and as wide as the tool, so the tools beside it do not move (a control never changes place between pages or states). It is out of the page for the keyboard and for screen readers.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Name of the group for screen readers («View»).

props.name: label
props.doc: The name of the search («Search the mail»): of the magnifier, of the field, and its placeholder.

props.name: value
props.doc: The text searched for.

props.name: open
props.doc: Open, when the app decides (its own key opens it). Absent: the toolbar keeps the state.

props.name: closed
props.doc: Closed, it is the magnifier alone (`icon`, the default) or a quiet field with its name and its key (`field`), for a bar where the search is the main way in. On a narrow bar the field is the magnifier too.

props.name: shortcut
props.doc: The key the app opens it with («Ctrl K»), shown in the hint. The app binds the key.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: The placeholder, if it differs from the name.

props.name: absent
props.doc: The search is not there in this view: its place stays, empty and as wide as it is closed, so the tools beside it do not move.

components.name: ToolbarSpacer
components.doc: Empty room that pushes what follows to the end of the bar; in a `TitleBar` it moves the window.

props.name: icon
props.doc: A 16px drawing before the word.

components.name: ToolbarTabs
components.doc: The views of the app, as words in a toolbar. They are places, not panels: the one the user is in is the current page.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Name of the views for screen readers («Views»).

props.name: value
props.doc: The view the user is in.

props.name: edge
props.doc: The edge of its bar the accent bar of the current view sits on: `bottom` (the default) for tabs in or under the title bar, `top` for tabs in a bar at the foot of the window.

props.name: size
props.doc: `sm` for tabs in a status bar: 12px words.

props.name: layout
props.doc: `stacked`: the icon over the word, each tab taking an equal share of the bar (a bottom bar on a narrow window).

components.name: ToolbarTitle
components.doc: The name of the window or of the place, in the bar: short of room it is cut with an ellipsis, down to 80px.

files.about:
Park UI (MIT) file-upload 102769c — recipe translated to Tailwind for @acaprino/sigrid (https://github.com/chakra-ui/park-ui/blob/102769c/packages/preset/src/recipes/file-upload.ts)

«Attachments» (a section of an entry's details): the list of the attachments and the zone to add one. From Park's `file-upload`
recipe comes the look: the zone on the raised sheet with l3 corners and a 2px dashed border that turns solid (in the
ink, R2) while something is dragged over it, two lines of text (no upload icon: the words say it, R6), and each
attachment a raised item with l3 corners and the xs shadow in place of Park's hairline (R4: file tiles get a shadow). The control rests on Ark UI's
FileUpload (`@ark-ui/react/file-upload`).
Ark gives: the button that opens the system picker and the `<input type="file">` behind it (outside the
accessibility tree and the Tab order, emptied before each choice so the same file can be chosen again), and the
check of every file against the limit (`maxFileSize`): the ones within it are accepted, the others rejected with
their reason. Its list of chosen files is kept empty: a file goes to `onAttach` at once and the list is the caller's
(`AttachmentView`), with thumbnail, state, «Open» and «Remove» that hand the actions back to `onAction`.
Ours: the drop (`useDropTarget`: Ark's dropzone takes files only and keeps every other drag for itself, while here a
link is an attachment too and dropped text is refused with a message; a dropped file goes through Ark's check like a
chosen one); the words, in English; the field for a typed link; focus after «Remove». No animation, no preview, no
network.

components.name: AttachmentMarks
components.doc: Indicator of the attachments on a row or a details sheet: one mark per kind and the number. Nothing at zero.

components.name: AttachmentsSection

files.about:
The form a person signs in or signs up with, the same in every app, in three forms: `signIn` (an address and a
password), `signUp` (the same, and a name when the app asks for one) and `link` (an address alone: the app sends a
link that opens the account, and the form then says to look in the inbox).
It asks for as little as it can: every field more costs people who would have signed up; what else the app needs
is asked after, when they are in (a `Wizard`).
Above the fields, when the app offers them, the accounts kept elsewhere («Continue with Acme»), each with its logo;
then the word «or», then the fields. One solid button (R3): the form's own. The way to the other form, and to a
forgotten password, are links under it.
What is wrong is said under the field it is about, when the form is sent, and the focus goes to the first such
field; a failure the server reports (`error`) is a note above the fields. While the app works (`busy`) the button
waits in its place. The form knows no server: it gives the app what was written and the app answers.

files.about:
A whole chat with an assistant, ready to wire to a model: the thread, what the assistant did on the way to each
answer, the ready-made requests and the field, put together the one way they go together. The app holds the
messages as data and talks to its model; the chat draws them and tells the app what the user did: sent a message,
stopped the answer, asked for it again, said it was good or not.
It is the parts of a conversation and nothing more (`Conversation`, `Message`, `Reasoning`, `ToolCall`,
`Suggestions`, `PromptInput`): an app whose chat needs another arrangement composes those itself.
What it decides, so every app's chat behaves alike: an answer still being written (`busy`, the last message) shows
no actions yet, and its reasoning is open until the text starts; «try again» is offered on the last answer only; a
failed answer is a `Note` with `tone="error"` in the thread, with «Try again»; a suggestion fills the field and
gives it the focus, for the user to send or change; the field keeps its text while an answer is written.

a window drawn in the theme the two colours make (`colorTheme`, with the colours as chosen): a chosen row with its
count, something due, something running and a button, so the person sees what each colour will be used for.

The spot is not picked from the whole wheel: three colours matched to the theme colour are proposed, from quiet to loud (`spotSuggestions`), besides none and one of the user's own. The sample below is drawn with the theme the two colours give (`colorTheme`).
